name: Afghanistan
famous_for: Silk Road crossroads, lapis lazuli gems, handwoven rugs, and Hindu Kush peaks.
tourists: Approx. 20,000 visitors; top sights include the Minaret of Jam and Blue Mosque of Mazar-i-Sharif.
must_know: Hospitality (Melmastia) is a sacred cultural code; remove shoes before entering traditional homes.
fun_fact: Buzkashi is the ancient national sport, an intense equestrian contest played on horseback.
short_desc: Silk Road crossroads, lapis lazuli gems, handwoven rugs, and Hindu Kush peaks.

name: Albania
famous_for: Albanian Riviera, UNESCO Ottoman stone towns of Berat & Gjirokastër, and Illyrian ruins.
tourists: Over 10.1M visitors; famous for Ksamil beaches, Blue Eye spring, and Rozafa Castle.
must_know: The ancient code of 'Besa' (sacred oath of hospitality) runs deep; nodding can mean 'no'.
fun_fact: Albania has over 173,000 concrete military defense bunkers built across its countryside.
short_desc: Albanian Riviera, UNESCO Ottoman stone towns of Berat & Gjirokastër, and Illyrian ruins.

name: Algeria
famous_for: Vast Sahara Desert dunes, Roman ruins of Timgad and Djemila, Casbah of Algiers, and Raï music.
tourists: Over 2.5M visitors; top attractions include Tassili n'Ajjer prehistoric rock art and Ghoufi canyon.
must_know: Hospitality is legendary; hosts will always prepare mint tea and dates for guests entering a home.
fun_fact: Algeria is the largest country in Africa and the tenth largest in the world by total land area.
short_desc: Vast Sahara Desert dunes, Roman ruins of Timgad and Djemila, Casbah of Algiers, and Raï music.

name: Angola
famous_for: Kalandula Falls, Serra da Leba pass, and vibrant Kizomba music and dance.
tourists: Approx. 210,000 visitors; highlights include Kalandula Falls and Quiçama National Park.
must_know: Greetings are warm and polite; handshakes are accompanied by asking about family welfare.
fun_fact: Angola is the birthplace of Kizomba, a world-famous sensual partner dance and music genre.
short_desc: Kalandula Falls, Serra da Leba pass, and vibrant Kizomba music and dance.

name: Antarctica
famous_for: Colossal ice shelves, Emperor penguin colonies, massive blue glaciers, and polar research.
tourists: Approx. 105,000 cruise visitors; famous for Lemaire Channel and Deception Island.
must_know: Strict biosecurity protocols mandate taking nothing and leaving nothing behind.
fun_fact: Antarctica holds about 70% of the world's fresh water and 90% of its ice, yet is the driest desert.
short_desc: Colossal ice shelves, Emperor penguin colonies, massive blue glaciers, and polar research.

name: Argentina
famous_for: Tango dancing, world-renowned Asado barbecues, Patagonia glaciers, and Mendoza Malbec wine.
tourists: Over 7.4M visitors; top sights include Iguazú Falls, Perito Moreno Glacier, and La Boca.
must_know: Sharing Mate herbal tea is an intimate communal bonding ritual; dinners start late after 9:30 PM.
fun_fact: Argentina has both the highest peak (Aconcagua, 6,961m) and lowest point in the Western Hemisphere.
short_desc: Tango dancing, world-renowned Asado barbecues, Patagonia glaciers, and Mendoza Malbec wine.

name: Armenia
famous_for: Ancient cliffside monasteries, Mount Ararat views, intricate khachkars, and lavash bread.
tourists: Over 2.3M visitors; highlights include Geghard Monastery, Lake Sevan, and Tatev cable car.
must_know: Hospitality to guests is considered a divine blessing; bread is held sacred and never placed upside down.
fun_fact: Armenia was the first nation in the world to adopt Christianity as its state religion in 301 AD.
short_desc: Ancient cliffside monasteries, Mount Ararat views, intricate khachkars, and lavash bread.

name: Australia
famous_for: Sydney Opera House, Great Barrier Reef, Uluru monolith, kangaroos & koalas, and beaches.
tourists: Over 9.5M visitors; famous for Bondi Beach, Great Ocean Road, and Daintree Rainforest.
must_know: 'No worries' embodies the friendly culture; sun protection is crucial under intense UV rays.
fun_fact: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest living organism structure on Earth, visible from space.
short_desc: Sydney Opera House, Great Barrier Reef, Uluru monolith, kangaroos & koalas, and beaches.

name: Austria
famous_for: Classical music (Mozart & Beethoven), snow-capped Alps, Schönbrunn Palace, and coffeehouses.
tourists: Over 31.9M visitors; highlights include Hallstatt lakeside village, Hofburg Palace, and alpine trails.
must_know: Viennese coffee house culture is UNESCO recognized; lingering for hours with a newspaper is celebrated.
fun_fact: Over 62% of Austria's landmass is covered by the Alps, making it an epic winter sports paradise.
short_desc: Classical music (Mozart & Beethoven), snow-capped Alps, Schönbrunn Palace, and coffeehouses.

name: Azerbaijan
famous_for: Flame Towers, historic Old Baku, Gobustan rock art, Yanar Dag burning flames, and Caspian caviar.
tourists: Over 2.1M visitors; top sights include Maiden Tower, Mud Volcanoes, and Sheki Khans' Palace.
must_know: Serving tea (Chay) in pear-shaped Armudu glasses with jam is a fundamental sign of hospitality.
fun_fact: Azerbaijan contains nearly half of all the mud volcanoes in the world, with over 400 bubbling mounds.
short_desc: Flame Towers, historic Old Baku, Gobustan rock art, Yanar Dag burning flames, and Caspian caviar.

name: Bangladesh
famous_for: The Sundarbans mangrove forest (Bengal Tigers), Cox's Bazar unbroken beach, and tea gardens.
tourists: Approx. 650,000 visitors; popular for Cox's Bazar, Lalbagh Fort, and Srimangal tea estates.
must_know: The 1952 Language Movement inspired UNESCO to declare February 21 Mother Language Day.
fun_fact: Cox's Bazar boasts a natural unbroken sandy sea beach stretching an astonishing 120 km (75 mi).
short_desc: The Sundarbans mangrove forest (Bengal Tigers), Cox's Bazar unbroken beach, and tea gardens.

name: Belarus
famous_for: Mir Castle, Nesvizh Palace, primeval Belovezhskaya Pushcha forest (European bison), and Soviet avenues.
tourists: Approx. 1.5M visitors; known for Braslaw Lakes, Brest Fortress, and Dudutki Folk Crafts Museum.
must_know: Bread and salt are traditionally offered to honored guests as a mark of warm welcoming and goodwill.
fun_fact: Belovezhskaya Pushcha is one of the last and largest remaining parts of primeval European lowland forest.
short_desc: Mir Castle, Nesvizh Palace, primeval Belovezhskaya Pushcha forest (European bison), and Soviet avenues.

name: Belgium
famous_for: Artisanal chocolates, medieval canals of Bruges, hundreds of craft beers, and crispy waffles.
tourists: Over 9.3M visitors; highlights include Grand Place, Atomium, Gravensteen Castle, and Bruges Belfry.
must_know: Divided into Dutch-speaking Flanders in the north and French-speaking Wallonia in the south.
fun_fact: Belgium produces over 220,000 tonnes of world-famous chocolate each year.
short_desc: Artisanal chocolates, medieval canals of Bruges, hundreds of craft beers, and crispy waffles.

name: Belize
famous_for: Belize Barrier Reef, Great Blue Hole marine sinkhole, ancient Maya ruins like Caracol, and Garifuna beats.
tourists: Over 1.7M visitors; popular for Ambergris Caye, Shark Ray Alley, and Actun Tunichil Muknal cave.
must_know: The official language is English, making it the only English-speaking nation in Central America.
fun_fact: The Great Blue Hole is an undersea sinkhole over 300 meters across and 124 meters deep.
short_desc: Belize Barrier Reef, Great Blue Hole marine sinkhole, ancient Maya ruins like Caracol, and Garifuna beats.

name: Benin
famous_for: Kingdom of Dahomey history, stilt city of Ganvié ('Venice of Africa'), and Vodun heritage.
tourists: Approx. 350,000 visitors; top attractions include Royal Palaces of Abomey and Ouidah Door of No Return.
must_know: Vodun is an officially recognized religion celebrated with nationwide festivals every January 10.
fun_fact: Ganvié is the largest stilt city in Africa, with roughly 20,000 people living entirely on the water.
short_desc: Kingdom of Dahomey history, stilt city of Ganvié ('Venice of Africa'), and Vodun heritage.

name: Bermuda
famous_for: Pink sand beaches of Horseshoe Bay, Bermuda shorts fashion, crystal caves, and shipwreck diving.
tourists: Over 650,000 visitors; known for Horseshoe Bay, Royal Naval Dockyard, and Gibbs Hill Lighthouse.
must_know: Bermuda shorts worn with knee-length socks and a blazer are considered formal business attire.
fun_fact: Bermuda has more shipwrecks per square mile than anywhere else on the planet.
short_desc: Pink sand beaches of Horseshoe Bay, Bermuda shorts fashion, crystal caves, and shipwreck diving.

name: Bhutan
famous_for: Tiger's Nest Monastery (Paro Taktsang), Gross National Happiness philosophy, and fortress dzongs.
tourists: Approx. 315,000 visitors; famous for Paro Taktsang, Punakha Dzong, and Dochula Pass stupas.
must_know: Smoking is strictly regulated; visitors must dress respectfully with covered shoulders and legs inside Dzongs.
fun_fact: Bhutan is the world's first carbon-negative country, absorbing more greenhouse gases than it emits.
short_desc: Tiger's Nest Monastery (Paro Taktsang), Gross National Happiness philosophy, and fortress dzongs.

name: Bolivia
famous_for: Salar de Uyuni salt flat (world's largest mirror), Lake Titicaca, cable cars, and colorful Cholita skirts.
tourists: Over 1.2M visitors; famous for Salar de Uyuni, North Yungas 'Death Road', and Tiwanaku ruins.
must_know: Bolivia has 37 official languages, including Spanish, Quechua, Aymara, and Guaraní.
fun_fact: Salar de Uyuni covers over 10,500 square kilometers and becomes the world's largest sky-reflecting mirror in rain.
short_desc: Salar de Uyuni salt flat (world's largest mirror), Lake Titicaca, cable cars, and colorful Cholita skirts.

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
famous_for: Stari Most (Old Bridge) in Mostar, historic Ottoman Baščaršija bazaar, and Balkan coffee tradition.
tourists: Over 1.7M visitors; highlights include Kravica Waterfalls, Sarajevo Old Town, and Blagaj Tekke monastery.
must_know: Drinking traditional Bosnian coffee (bosanska kafa) from a copper dzezva with rahat lokum is an unhurried ritual.
fun_fact: Sarajevo was the first city in Europe to have a full-time operational electric tram network in 1885.
short_desc: Stari Most (Old Bridge) in Mostar, historic Ottoman Baščaršija bazaar, and Balkan coffee tradition.

name: Botswana
famous_for: Okavango Delta, Kalahari Desert, dense elephant herds of Chobe National Park, and luxury eco-safaris.
tourists: Over 1.8M visitors; highlights include Okavango Delta mokoro canoe trips and Chobe boat cruises.
must_know: The national currency 'Pula' literally means 'Rain', signifying how precious rain is in the country.
fun_fact: Botswana is home to the world's largest concentration of African elephants, with over 130,000 individuals.
short_desc: Okavango Delta, Kalahari Desert, dense elephant herds of Chobe National Park, and luxury eco-safaris.

name: Brazil
famous_for: Rio Carnival, Amazon Rainforest, Christ the Redeemer statue, Copacabana beach, and Samba rhythms.
tourists: Over 6.6M visitors; top attractions include Iguazu Falls, Rio beaches, and the Amazon river basin.
must_know: Hugging and cheek-kisses are customary greetings; Brazilians radiate infectious warmth and joy.
fun_fact: The Amazon Rainforest in Brazil produces roughly 20% of the world's oxygen and holds 10% of all species.
short_desc: Rio Carnival, Amazon Rainforest, Christ the Redeemer statue, Copacabana beach, and Samba rhythms.

name: Brunei
famous_for: Gold-domed Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque, Kampong Ayer water village, and virgin Borneo rainforest.
tourists: Over 300,000 visitors; top sights include Jame' Asr Mosque and Ulu Temburong National Park.
must_know: Pointing with the index finger is impolite; locals gesture with the right thumb over folded fingers.
fun_fact: Istana Nurul Iman in Brunei is the world's largest residential palace, with 1,788 rooms.
short_desc: Gold-domed Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque, Kampong Ayer water village, and virgin Borneo rainforest.

name: Bulgaria
famous_for: Rose Valley oil production, Rila Monastery, Black Sea resorts, and Roman ruins in Plovdiv.
tourists: Over 8.9M visitors; highlights include Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, Belogradchik Rocks, and Bansko ski slopes.
must_know: In Bulgaria, nodding up and down often means 'no', while shaking the head side-to-side means 'yes'.
fun_fact: Bulgaria produces up to 85% of the world's rose oil, an essential raw ingredient in luxury perfumery.
short_desc: Rose Valley oil production, Rila Monastery, Black Sea resorts, and Roman ruins in Plovdiv.

name: Burkina Faso
famous_for: FESPACO cinema festival, Sindou rock peaks, bronze crafts, and Tiébélé painted houses.
tourists: Approx. 180,000 visitors; famous for Cascades de Karfiguéla and Grand Mosque of Bobo-Dioulasso.
must_know: The country's name translates to 'Land of Incorruptible People' (Burkina = upright, Faso = homeland).
fun_fact: Tiébélé village is celebrated for elaborate, hand-painted geometric mural houses made by Kassena women.
short_desc: FESPACO cinema festival, Sindou rock peaks, bronze crafts, and Tiébélé painted houses.

name: Burundi
famous_for: Royal Drummers of Burundi, Lake Tanganyika shores, lush tea hills, and Rusizi National Park.
tourists: Approx. 150,000 visitors; known for Lake Tanganyika beaches, Karera Falls, and Gishora Drum Sanctuary.
must_know: The sacred ritual drumming of royal drums is inscribed on the UNESCO Cultural Heritage list.
fun_fact: Burundi borders Lake Tanganyika, the world's second-deepest and second-largest freshwater lake by volume.
short_desc: Royal Drummers of Burundi, Lake Tanganyika shores, lush tea hills, and Rusizi National Park.

name: Cambodia
famous_for: Angkor Wat (world's largest religious monument), ornate Khmer stone carvings, Tonlé Sap floating villages, and Apsara dance.
tourists: Over 6.6M visitors; famous for Bayon temple with giant stone smiling faces, Ta Prohm tree root temple, and Royal Palace.
must_know: The traditional 'Sampeah' greeting involves pressing both palms together at chest level with a respectful nod.
fun_fact: Angkor Wat spans over 162.6 hectares and was originally constructed in the early 12th century as a Hindu temple dedicated to Vishnu.
short_desc: Angkor Wat (world's largest religious monument), ornate Khmer stone carvings, Tonlé Sap floating villages, and Apsara dance.

name: Cameroon
famous_for: 'Africa in Miniature' for diverse climates, Mount Cameroon volcano, Makossa music, and Indomitable Lions.
tourists: Over 1.1M visitors; famous for Mount Cameroon, Waza National Park, and Kribi white-sand waterfalls.
must_know: Both English and French are official languages, reflecting its dual colonial administrative heritage.
fun_fact: The Lobé Waterfalls near Kribi are among the very few waterfalls on Earth that tumble directly into the ocean.
short_desc: 'Africa in Miniature' for diverse climates, Mount Cameroon volcano, Makossa music, and Indomitable Lions.

name: Canada
famous_for: Niagara Falls, turquoise glacial lakes of Banff & Jasper, Maple syrup, ice hockey, and polite society.
tourists: Over 22.1M visitors; famous for Lake Louise, CN Tower, Old Quebec, and Whistler ski slopes.
must_know: Apologizing ('sorry') is so common in Canadian manners that Ontario passed the Apology Act.
fun_fact: Canada has the longest coastline in the world, stretching over 243,042 kilometers across three oceans.
short_desc: Niagara Falls, turquoise glacial lakes of Banff & Jasper, Maple syrup, ice hockey, and polite society.

name: Central African Republic
famous_for: Dzanga-Ndoki National Park, western lowland gorillas, forest elephants, and Boali Waterfalls.
tourists: Approx. 110,000 visitors; famous for Dzanga Bai ('village of elephants') and Chutes de Boali.
must_know: Sango is spoken as a widespread lingua franca across all ethnic communities alongside French.
fun_fact: Dzanga Bai in the dense rainforest attracts hundreds of forest elephants simultaneously to mineral muds.
short_desc: Dzanga-Ndoki National Park, western lowland gorillas, forest elephants, and Boali Waterfalls.

name: Chad
famous_for: Ennedi Plateau desert sandstone arches and gueltas, Lake Chad waters, and Zakouma National Park elephant herds.
tourists: Approx. 90,000 desert adventurers; famous for Guelta d'Archei desert camel pool and Tibesti volcanic peaks.
must_know: Guelta d'Archei in the Ennedi Plateau is a dramatic desert canyon where hundreds of camels drink alongside rare dwarf Saharan crocodiles.
fun_fact: Chad is named after Lake Chad, which was once a colossal prehistoric inland sea dubbed 'Mega-Chad' covering 350,000 square km.
short_desc: Ennedi Plateau desert sandstone arches and gueltas, Lake Chad waters, and Zakouma National Park elephant herds.

name: Chile
famous_for: Atacama Desert (driest on Earth), Torres del Paine granite peaks in Patagonia, Moai statues, and wine.
tourists: Over 4.5M visitors; top sights include Torres del Paine, San Pedro de Atacama, and Valparaíso.
must_know: The Cueca is the spirited national courtship dance, danced with handkerchiefs twirled in the air.
fun_fact: Chile is the longest north-to-south country in the world, extending 4,270 km while averaging 177 km wide.
short_desc: Atacama Desert (driest on Earth), Torres del Paine granite peaks in Patagonia, Moai statues, and wine.

name: China
famous_for: The Great Wall of China, Forbidden City, Terracotta Army, giant pandas, and high-speed bullet trains.
tourists: Over 65.7M visitors; famous for Great Wall, Zhangjiajie peaks, and Li River karst hills in Guilin.
must_know: Always accept and present business cards or gifts using both hands as an essential sign of respect.
fun_fact: China's high-speed rail network exceeds 45,000 kilometers, longer than the rest of the world combined.
short_desc: The Great Wall of China, Forbidden City, Terracotta Army, giant pandas, and high-speed bullet trains.

name: Colombia
famous_for: Specialty coffee, unmatched bird biodiversity, walled Caribbean Cartagena, Cumbia & Salsa rhythms.
tourists: Over 4.5M visitors; famous for Cartagena Old Town, Coffee Triangle (Eje Cafetero), and Tayrona Park.
must_know: Greeting with a warm handshake and asking about someone's day is essential courtesy across Colombia.
fun_fact: Colombia is home to Caño Cristales, known as the 'Liquid Rainbow' due to endemic bright red river plants.
short_desc: Specialty coffee, unmatched bird biodiversity, walled Caribbean Cartagena, Cumbia & Salsa rhythms.

name: Costa Rica
famous_for: 'Pura Vida' peaceful lifestyle, Arenal Volcano, Monteverde cloud forest, sloths, and no standing army.
tourists: Over 3.3M visitors; top sights include Manuel Antonio National Park, Tortuguero canals, and hot springs.
must_know: 'Pura Vida' (pure life) serves as hello, goodbye, thank you, and a peaceful everyday state of mind.
fun_fact: Despite covering only 0.03% of the Earth's surface, Costa Rica holds roughly 5% of all biodiversity.
short_desc: 'Pura Vida' peaceful lifestyle, Arenal Volcano, Monteverde cloud forest, sloths, and no standing army.

name: Croatia
famous_for: Walled medieval city of Dubrovnik ('Pearl of the Adriatic'), Plitvice Lakes cascading waterfalls, and Dalmatian coast.
tourists: Over 20.6M international visitors; famous for Dubrovnik city walls, Diocletian's Palace in Split, and Hvar island.
must_know: The necktie (cravat) originated in Croatia: 17th-century Croatian mercenaries tied knotted scarves that fascinated King Louis XIV.
fun_fact: Dubrovnik's medieval fortifications and orange-roofed alleys famously served as King's Landing in Game of Thrones.
short_desc: Walled medieval city of Dubrovnik ('Pearl of the Adriatic'), Plitvice Lakes cascading waterfalls, and Dalmatian coast.

name: Cuba
famous_for: Classic 1950s American vintage cars, Habano cigars, Salsa & Son Cubano music, and Old Havana.
tourists: Over 2.4M visitors; highlights include Havana Malecón, Viñales tobacco valley, and Trinidad cobblestones.
must_know: Music is omnipresent in daily life; people regularly dance in plazas and living rooms to clave rhythms.
fun_fact: Cuba has one of the highest doctor-to-population ratios in the world and sends medical teams abroad.
short_desc: Classic 1950s American vintage cars, Habano cigars, Salsa & Son Cubano music, and Old Havana.

name: Cyprus
famous_for: Birthplace of Aphrodite (Petra tou Romiou), halloumi cheese, Troodos painted churches, and beaches.
tourists: Over 3.8M tourists; famous for Paphos Roman mosaics, Cape Greco sea caves, and Ayia Napa beaches.
must_know: Halloumi cheese has protected designation of origin (PDO) status; it can be grilled without melting.
fun_fact: Cyprus is home to Commandaria, the world's oldest named wine still in active continuous production.
short_desc: Birthplace of Aphrodite (Petra tou Romiou), halloumi cheese, Troodos painted churches, and beaches.

name: Czech Republic
famous_for: Fairytale Prague Castle, Charles Bridge, historic Pilsner brewing, and Bohemian crystal glassware.
tourists: Over 19.5M visitors; top attractions include Prague Astronomical Clock, Kutná Hora, and Český Krumlov.
must_know: Czechs drink more beer per capita than any other nation (over 180 liters per person annually).
fun_fact: Prague Castle is recognized by the Guinness World Records as the largest ancient castle complex in the world.
short_desc: Fairytale Prague Castle, Charles Bridge, historic Pilsner brewing, and Bohemian crystal glassware.

name: DR Congo
famous_for: Congo River Basin rainforest, mountain gorillas in Virunga, Nyiragongo lava lake, and Rumba music.
tourists: Approx. 250,000 visitors; top destinations include Virunga National Park and Mount Nyiragongo.
must_know: Congolese Rumba is UNESCO recognized; the elegant Sapeurs (La Sape) dress in flamboyant haute couture.
fun_fact: Mount Nyiragongo houses the world's largest churning persistent molten lava lake in its crater.
short_desc: Congo River Basin rainforest, mountain gorillas in Virunga, Nyiragongo lava lake, and Rumba music.

name: Denmark
famous_for: 'Hygge' cozy living philosophy, bicycle culture, Lego bricks, Hans Christian Andersen tales, and New Nordic food.
tourists: Over 15.2M visitors; highlights include Nyhavn harbor, Tivoli Gardens, and Kronborg Castle ('Hamlet's Castle').
must_know: 'Hygge' represents cozy, contented well-being shared over candlelight, coffee, pastries, and good friends.
fun_fact: Copenhagen is one of the world's premier cycling capitals, where over 60% of residents commute by bike.
short_desc: 'Hygge' cozy living philosophy, bicycle culture, Lego bricks, Hans Christian Andersen tales, and New Nordic food.

name: Djibouti
famous_for: Lake Assal (lowest point in Africa), swimming with whale sharks in Gulf of Tadjoura, and salt flats.
tourists: Approx. 140,000 visitors; famous for Lake Abbé volcanic chimneys and Day Forest National Park.
must_know: Chewing Khat in the afternoon is a customary social habit shared among men discussing community matters.
fun_fact: Lake Assal is the lowest point in Africa (-155m) and the second-saltest body of water on Earth after Don Juan Pond.
short_desc: Lake Assal (lowest point in Africa), swimming with whale sharks in Gulf of Tadjoura, and salt flats.

name: Dominican Republic
famous_for: Punta Cana white beaches, Merengue and Bachata dance rhythms, colonial Zona Colonial, and baseball.
tourists: Over 10.3M tourists; famous for Saona Island, Samaná whale watching, and Pico Duarte peak.
must_know: Merengue and Bachata were born here and are UNESCO inscribed as intangible cultural heritage.
fun_fact: The Zona Colonial in Santo Domingo holds the first cathedral, paved street, and university in the Americas.
short_desc: Punta Cana white beaches, Merengue and Bachata dance rhythms, colonial Zona Colonial, and baseball.

name: East Timor
famous_for: Atauro Island (world's most biodiverse coral reef system), Christo Rei monument, Mount Ramelau sacred sunrise, and Tais woven textiles.
tourists: Approx. 80,000 visitors; famous for Atauro Island diving, Jaco Island uninhabited beach, and Dare memorial museum.
must_know: In Timorese culture, the saltwater crocodile is revered as the sacred ancestor 'Lafaek' who formed the island of Timor according to creation myth.
fun_fact: Marine surveys conducted around Atauro Island discovered the highest average reef fish diversity per dive anywhere on Earth.
short_desc: Atauro Island (world's most biodiverse coral reef system), Christo Rei monument, Mount Ramelau sacred sunrise, and Tais woven textiles.

name: Ecuador
famous_for: Galápagos Islands (Darwin's finches & giant tortoises), Cotopaxi active volcano, and Otavalo markets.
tourists: Over 2.1M visitors; famous for Galapagos wildlife cruises, historic Quito Old Town, and Quilotoa crater lake.
must_know: Quito was the first city in the world to be declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1978.
fun_fact: Mount Chimborazo's summit is the closest point on the Earth's surface to the Sun due to equatorial bulge.
short_desc: Galápagos Islands (Darwin's finches & giant tortoises), Cotopaxi active volcano, and Otavalo markets.

name: Egypt
famous_for: The Great Pyramids of Giza, Great Sphinx, the Nile River, Valley of the Kings, and Tutankhamun.
tourists: Over 14.9M international tourists annually; famous for Karnak Temple, Abu Simbel, and Red Sea coral diving.
must_know: Always use the right hand for eating and greeting; Egyptians appreciate respectful compliments and humor.
fun_fact: The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest man-made structure in the world for over 3,800 years.
short_desc: The Great Pyramids of Giza, Great Sphinx, the Nile River, Valley of the Kings, and Tutankhamun.

name: El Salvador
famous_for: Pupusas (stuffed griddled masa cakes), world-class surf point breaks of El Tunco, Santa Ana volcano crater lake, and Ruta de las Flores.
tourists: Over 3.4M visitors; highlights include Joya de Cerén ('Pompeii of the Americas'), Coatepeque caldera lake, and Tazumal Maya ruins.
must_know: The Pupusa is the beloved national dish: a thick griddled corn cake stuffed with quesillo cheese, chicharrón, or loroco edible flowers.
fun_fact: Joya de Cerén was buried under volcanic ash around 600 AD, preserving an intact pre-Columbian Maya farming village.
short_desc: Pupusas (stuffed griddled masa cakes), world-class surf point breaks of El Tunco, Santa Ana volcano crater lake, and Ruta de las Flores.

name: Equatorial Guinea
famous_for: Bioko Island volcanic peaks, black sand beaches, colonial Spanish architecture, and Monte Alén cloud forest.
tourists: Approx. 85,000 visitors; top destinations include Malabo cathedral, Arena Blanca butterfly beach, and Pico Basile peak.
must_know: It is the only sovereign country in Africa where Spanish is an official primary language.
fun_fact: The capital city, Malabo, is situated on the volcanic island of Bioko, rather than on the African mainland territory (Río Muni).
short_desc: Bioko Island volcanic peaks, black sand beaches, colonial Spanish architecture, and Monte Alén cloud forest.

name: Eritrea
famous_for: UNESCO modernist Art Deco Italian architecture in Asmara, Dahlak Archipelago corals, and coffee ceremonies.
tourists: Approx. 145,000 visitors; known for Asmara modernist buildings, Massawa Ottoman port, and Qohaito ruins.
must_know: The traditional Eritrean coffee ceremony involves roasting raw green beans over coals and boiling in a jebena pot.
fun_fact: Asmara is nicknamed 'Piccola Roma' (Little Rome) for its world-class ensemble of 1930s futuristic architecture.
short_desc: UNESCO modernist Art Deco Italian architecture in Asmara, Dahlak Archipelago corals, and coffee ceremonies.

name: Estonia
famous_for: Medieval fairytale Old Town of Tallinn, advanced e-government digital society, bog walks, and smoke saunas.
tourists: Over 3.5M visitors; top attractions include Tallinn Town Hall Square, Lahemaa National Park, and Saaremaa island.
must_know: Estonia is the most digital society on Earth: 99% of government services, voting, and taxes are handled online.
fun_fact: Estonia's ancient UNESCO-inscribed smoke sauna tradition requires hours of slow heating and birch branch whisking.
short_desc: Medieval fairytale Old Town of Tallinn, advanced e-government digital society, bog walks, and smoke saunas.

name: Eswatini
famous_for: Kingdom of Eswatini royal traditions, Umhlanga Reed Dance festival, Mlilwane Wildlife Sanctuary, and glass-blowing crafts.
tourists: Over 1.2M visitors; famous for Umhlanga Reed Dance at Ludzidzini royal kraal, Ngwenya glass factory, and Mantenga cultural village.
must_know: Eswatini is one of the world's last remaining absolute monarchies, ruled by the Ngwenyama (King) alongside the Ndlovukati (Queen Mother).
fun_fact: Ngwenya Mine in northwestern Eswatini contains iron ore workings dating back 43,000 years, the oldest known mine on Earth.
short_desc: Kingdom of Eswatini royal traditions, Umhlanga Reed Dance festival, Mlilwane Wildlife Sanctuary, and glass-blowing crafts.

name: Ethiopia
famous_for: Rock-hewn monolithic churches of Lalibela, birthplace of Arabica coffee, Simien Mountains, and Lucy fossil.
tourists: Approx. 900,000 visitors; famous for Lalibela rock churches, Danakil Depression lava, and Gondar castles.
must_know: Ethiopia operates on its own ancient calendar with 13 months, lagging roughly 7 years behind the Gregorian calendar.
fun_fact: Ethiopia is the only African nation that successfully defeated European colonizers (Battle of Adwa in 1896).
short_desc: Rock-hewn monolithic churches of Lalibela, birthplace of Arabica coffee, Simien Mountains, and Lucy fossil.

name: Falkland Islands
famous_for: Massive penguin colonies (King, Gentoo, Magellanic, Rockhopper), albatrosses, and rugged South Atlantic moors.
tourists: Over 70,000 cruise visitors annually; popular for Volunteer Point king penguins and Gypsy Cove.
must_know: Sheep outnumber humans on the islands by roughly 150 to 1, with world-class Merino wool production.
fun_fact: Volunteer Point is home to the largest and most accessible King penguin breeding colony in the South Atlantic.
short_desc: Massive penguin colonies (King, Gentoo, Magellanic, Rockhopper), albatrosses, and rugged South Atlantic moors.

name: Fiji
famous_for: Idyllic South Pacific coral islands, warm 'Bula!' hospitality, Meke dance, kava ceremonies, and rugby sevens.
tourists: Over 920,000 visitors; famous for Mamanuca and Yasawa islands, Coral Coast, and Great Astrolabe Reef.
must_know: The traditional Kava (yaqona) ceremony is an important welcoming ritual where guests clap once before drinking.
fun_fact: Fiji was the first country to win back-to-back Olympic gold medals in Men's Rugby Sevens (Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020).
short_desc: Idyllic South Pacific coral islands, warm 'Bula!' hospitality, Meke dance, kava ceremonies, and rugby sevens.

name: Finland
famous_for: World's happiest country, Santa Claus Village in Lapland, Northern Lights, sauna culture, and 188,000 lakes.
tourists: Over 7.0M visitors; highlights include Rovaniemi winter village, Suomenlinna sea fortress, and Saimaa lake district.
must_know: Sauna is a fundamental way of life: there are over 3 million saunas in Finland, more than one for every two residents.
fun_fact: Finland has been officially ranked the World's Happiest Country by the United Nations for seven consecutive years.
short_desc: World's happiest country, Santa Claus Village in Lapland, Northern Lights, sauna culture, and 188,000 lakes.

name: France
famous_for: Eiffel Tower, Louvre Museum, haute cuisine, Champagne & Bordeaux wines, haute couture fashion, and French Riviera.
tourists: Over 100M international tourists annually (the world's most visited country); famous for Versailles and Mont Saint-Michel.
must_know: Greeting shopkeepers with a polite 'Bonjour, Madame/Monsieur' before asking a question is essential French etiquette.
fun_fact: France produces more than 1,200 distinct varieties of cheese and protects hundreds with strict AOC appellations.
short_desc: Eiffel Tower, Louvre Museum, haute cuisine, Champagne & Bordeaux wines, haute couture fashion, and French Riviera.

name: French Guiana
famous_for: Guiana Space Centre (Europe's spaceport in Kourou), pristine Amazonian rainforest, and Devil's Island penal colony.
tourists: Approx. 120,000 visitors; famous for watching Ariane rocket launches, Îles du Salut, and Amazon river safaris.
must_know: As an overseas department of France, French Guiana is an integral part of the European Union and uses the Euro.
fun_fact: The Guiana Space Centre in Kourou is ideally situated just 5 degrees north of the equator, maximizing rocket orbital velocity.
short_desc: Guiana Space Centre (Europe's spaceport in Kourou), pristine Amazonian rainforest, and Devil's Island penal colony.

name: French Southern Lands
famous_for: Remote sub-Antarctic volcanic islands, King penguin colonies, and elephant seals.
tourists: Scientific expedition visits; accessed primarily by the research ship Marion Dufresne.
must_know: Nature reserve status requires strict scientific clearance to set foot on the islands.
fun_fact: Home to the Kerguelen Islands, known as 'Desolation Islands' due to their remote Southern Ocean isolation.
short_desc: Remote sub-Antarctic volcanic islands, King penguin colonies, and elephant seals.

name: Gabon
famous_for: Loango National Park ('Africa's Last Eden' with surfing hippos), pristine rainforests, and mandrills.
tourists: Approx. 190,000 visitors; famous for surfing hippos on Loango beaches and Ivindo Waterfalls.
must_know: Over 10% of Gabon's entire land territory is protected within 13 magnificent national parks.
fun_fact: Gabon's Atlantic beaches in Loango are one of the only places on Earth where wild forest elephants and hippos wander on ocean sands.
short_desc: Loango National Park ('Africa's Last Eden' with surfing hippos), pristine rainforests, and mandrills.

name: Georgia
famous_for: Birthplace of wine (8,000-year Qvevri method), Caucasus mountain towers of Svaneti, and Khachapuri cheese bread.
tourists: Over 7.1M visitors; highlights include Gergeti Trinity Church below Mount Kazbek, Vardzia cave city, and Old Tbilisi sulfur baths.
must_know: The 'Supra' is a traditional feast led by a toastmaster (Tamada) celebrating life with elaborate philosophical toasts.
fun_fact: Archaeologists in Georgia discovered ceramic jars with wine residue dating back 8,000 years (6,000 BC).
short_desc: Birthplace of wine (8,000-year Qvevri method), Caucasus mountain towers of Svaneti, and Khachapuri cheese bread.

name: Germany
famous_for: Oktoberfest, Autobahn, Neuschwanstein Castle, engineering precision (BMW/Porsche), and Black Forest.
tourists: Over 39.6M international visitors; famous for Brandenburg Gate, Cologne Cathedral, and Bavarian Alps.
must_know: Directness and punctuality are deeply valued; jaywalking at red pedestrian lights is strongly frowned upon.
fun_fact: Germany has over 20,000 castles scattered across its landscapes, including fairytale Neuschwanstein.
short_desc: Oktoberfest, Autobahn, Neuschwanstein Castle, engineering precision (BMW/Porsche), and Black Forest.

name: Ghana
famous_for: Cape Coast slave castle history, colorful handwoven Kente cloth, Ashanti Kingdom heritage, and highlife music.
tourists: Over 1.1M visitors; famous for Kakum rainforest canopy walkway, Elmina Castle, and Labadi Beach.
must_know: Akwaaba means 'Welcome' and reflects the deeply ingrained warmth and hospitality given to all visitors.
fun_fact: Lake Volta in Ghana is the largest artificial reservoir in the world by surface area, covering 8,502 square km.
short_desc: Cape Coast slave castle history, colorful handwoven Kente cloth, Ashanti Kingdom heritage, and highlife music.

name: Greece
famous_for: Acropolis of Athens, birthplace of democracy and philosophy, whitewashed Santorini cliff villages, and Aegean islands.
tourists: Over 33.0M international tourists annually; famous for Parthenon, Meteora cliff monasteries, and Crete gorges.
must_know: Spitting playfully three times ('ftou ftou ftou') is a cultural custom to ward off the evil eye (mati) when complimenting someone.
fun_fact: Greece has thousands of islands, of which roughly 227 are inhabited, with an unbroken coastline of over 13,676 kilometers.
short_desc: Acropolis of Athens, birthplace of democracy and philosophy, whitewashed Santorini cliff villages, and Aegean islands.

name: Greenland
famous_for: Ilulissat Icefjord (birthplace of Titanic icebergs), dog sledding, Northern Lights, Midnight Sun, and Inuit culture.
tourists: Over 100,000 visitors annually; famous for UNESCO Ilulissat Icefjord, Disko Bay whale safaris, and Nuuk fjord.
must_know: Greenland is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark and the world's largest non-continental island.
fun_fact: Roughly 80% of Greenland's massive land surface is covered by a permanent ice sheet up to 3 kilometers thick.
short_desc: Ilulissat Icefjord (birthplace of Titanic icebergs), dog sledding, Northern Lights, Midnight Sun, and Inuit culture.

name: Guatemala
famous_for: Colossal Maya pyramids of Tikal hidden in the jungle, volcanic Lake Atitlán, and cobblestone colonial Antigua.
tourists: Over 2.6M visitors; famous for Tikal National Park, Semuc Champey turquoise pools, and Acatenango volcano hikes.
must_know: Handwoven traditional Huipil blouses feature intricate woven symbols identifying the weaver's hometown and ancestral lineage.
fun_fact: The Quetzal bird is sacred in Maya myth, the national bird and currency; in captivity, it was said to die of a broken heart.
short_desc: Colossal Maya pyramids of Tikal hidden in the jungle, volcanic Lake Atitlán, and cobblestone colonial Antigua.

name: Guinea
famous_for: Fouta Djallon highlands ('water tower of West Africa'), Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve, and djembe drumming.
tourists: Approx. 120,000 visitors; known for Chutes de Kinkon waterfalls, Iles de Los, and Mount Nimba chimpanzees.
must_know: Guinea is the ancestral heartland of the Djembe goblet drum, an instrument that spread to music halls worldwide.
fun_fact: The Niger, Senegal, and Gambia rivers—three of West Africa's greatest waterways—all originate in Guinea's Fouta Djallon.
short_desc: Fouta Djallon highlands ('water tower of West Africa'), Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve, and djembe drumming.

name: Guinea-Bissau
famous_for: The pristine Bijagós Archipelago (UNESCO Biosphere Reserve with saltwater hippos), and vibrant Portuguese-creole culture.
tourists: Approx. 60,000 visitors; famous for saltwater hippos in Orango National Park and Bissau Carnival.
must_know: The Bijagós Archipelago still preserves a matriarchal clan society where women hold immense social and religious leadership.
fun_fact: Orango National Park in Bijagós is one of the only places on Earth where hippos spend hours bathing in ocean surf.
short_desc: The pristine Bijagós Archipelago (UNESCO Biosphere Reserve with saltwater hippos), and vibrant Portuguese-creole culture.

name: Guyana
famous_for: Kaieteur Falls (world's largest single-drop waterfall), virgin Amazon rainforest, and English-speaking Caribbean culture.
tourists: Over 315,000 visitors; highlights include Kaieteur Falls, Rupununi savanna safaris, and Iwokrama rainforest canopy walkway.
must_know: Guyana is the only nation on the South American mainland where English is the official national language.
fun_fact: Kaieteur Falls drops 226 meters (741 ft) in a thunderous single vertical plume, five times higher than Niagara Falls.
short_desc: Kaieteur Falls (world's largest single-drop waterfall), virgin Amazon rainforest, and English-speaking Caribbean culture.

name: Haiti
famous_for: Citadelle Laferrière fortress, Sans-Souci Palace, colorful naive folk painting, and the world's first Black republic.
tourists: Approx. 400,000 visitors; famous for Citadelle Laferrière, Bassin Bleu waterfall, and Jacmel artisan carnival.
must_know: Haiti made history in 1804 by becoming the first country in the world founded through a successful slave revolution.
fun_fact: Citadelle Laferrière, perched 900 meters atop Bonnet à l'Évêque mountain, is the largest fortress in the Americas.
short_desc: Citadelle Laferrière fortress, Sans-Souci Palace, colorful naive folk painting, and the world's first Black republic.

name: Honduras
famous_for: Roatán coral reef diving in the Bay Islands, ancient Maya ruins of Copán with hieroglyphic stairway, and Baleadas.
tourists: Over 2.2M visitors; top attractions include West Bay beach in Roatán, Copán Ruinas, and Pico Bonito National Park.
must_know: The Baleada—a thick handmade flour tortilla folded over refried beans, queso duro, and mantequilla—is a national culinary staple.
fun_fact: Copán contains the Hieroglyphic Stairway, boasting the longest known inscribed Maya hieroglyphic text in the Americas.
short_desc: Roatán coral reef diving in the Bay Islands, ancient Maya ruins of Copán with hieroglyphic stairway, and Baleadas.

name: Hungary
famous_for: Budapest Parliament building along the Danube, natural thermal baths (Széchenyi), spicy Goulash, and Tokaji sweet wine.
tourists: Over 17.5M tourists annually; famous for Buda Castle, Chain Bridge, Lake Balaton, and ruined ruin-bars.
must_know: Clinking beer glasses during a toast was avoided for 150 years in Hungary following the 1849 Austrian execution of martyrs.
fun_fact: Budapest has over 120 natural geothermal springs delivering more than 70 million liters of warm thermal water every day.
short_desc: Budapest Parliament building along the Danube, natural thermal baths (Széchenyi), spicy Goulash, and Tokaji sweet wine.

name: Iceland
famous_for: 'Land of Fire and Ice', active erupting volcanoes, geothermal Blue Lagoon, cascading waterfalls, and glowing Northern Lights.
tourists: Over 2.2M international tourists annually; famous for the Golden Circle, Gullfoss waterfall, and black sand beach of Reynisfjara.
must_know: Icelanders can read their ancient 1,000-year-old Norse sagas almost effortlessly because the language has barely changed since settlement.
fun_fact: Iceland runs on nearly 100% renewable energy, powered almost entirely by natural geothermal steam and hydroelectric rivers.
short_desc: 'Land of Fire and Ice', active erupting volcanoes, geothermal Blue Lagoon, cascading waterfalls, and glowing Northern Lights.

name: India
famous_for: Taj Mahal wonder, vibrant Holi & Diwali festivals, Himalayan peaks, Yoga, rich spices, and ancient Ayurvedic wisdom.
tourists: Over 10.9M international tourists annually; famous for Jaipur Golden Triangle, Varanasi ghats, Kerala backwaters, and Goa beaches.
must_know: Joining hands in 'Namaste' with a slight bow is the revered sign of greeting that recognizes the divine essence within another.
fun_fact: India is the birthplace of four major world religions: Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and Sikhism.
short_desc: Taj Mahal wonder, vibrant Holi & Diwali festivals, Himalayan peaks, Yoga, rich spices, and ancient Ayurvedic wisdom.

name: Indonesia
famous_for: Bali tropical temples, Komodo dragons, Borobudur (largest Buddhist temple on Earth), volcanic landscapes, and Batik textiles.
tourists: Over 11.7M international tourists annually; famous for Ubud terraces, Raja Ampat diving, and Mount Bromo sunrise.
must_know: Always eat, hand gifts, and greet using the right hand; touching someone's head is taboo as it is considered spiritually sacred.
fun_fact: Indonesia is the largest archipelago nation on the planet, consisting of over 17,500 distinct tropical islands.
short_desc: Bali tropical temples, Komodo dragons, Borobudur (largest Buddhist temple on Earth), volcanic landscapes, and Batik textiles.

name: Iran
famous_for: Ancient ruins of Persepolis, Persian turquoise-tiled mosques in Isfahan, intricate hand-knotted rugs, and Hafez poetry.
tourists: Approx. 4.1M visitors; famous for Naqsh-e Jahan Square, Pink Mosque (Nasir al-Mulk), and Yazd desert wind-catchers.
must_know: 'Taarof' is an intricate cultural ritual of politeness where people defer to each other out of deep respect before accepting an offer.
fun_fact: Persepolis was the ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Persian Empire under Darius the Great around 518 BC.
short_desc: Ancient ruins of Persepolis, Persian turquoise-tiled mosques in Isfahan, intricate hand-knotted rugs, and Hafez poetry.

name: Iraq
famous_for: Ancient Mesopotamia ('Cradle of Civilization'), Babylon ruins, Ziggurat of Ur, Tigris and Euphrates rivers, and Mesopotamian Marshes.
tourists: Approx. 1.2M visitors (mostly pilgrims and heritage explorers); highlights include Citadel of Erbil and Holy Shrines of Karbala.
must_know: Mesopotamia is where humans first developed the wheel, written script (cuneiform), legal codes (Hammurabi), and mathematics.
fun_fact: The Citadel of Erbil is considered one of the oldest continuously inhabited human settlements on Earth, dating back 6,000 years.
short_desc: Ancient Mesopotamia ('Cradle of Civilization'), Babylon ruins, Ziggurat of Ur, Tigris and Euphrates rivers, and Mesopotamian Marshes.

name: Ireland
famous_for: Emerald green landscapes, Cliffs of Moher, Guinness stout brewing, traditional fiddle music pub sessions, and literary heritage.
tourists: Over 11.2M visitors; highlights include Ring of Kerry, Trinity College Long Room Library, and Giant's Causeway in nearby north.
must_know: 'Craic' is the quintessential Irish concept meaning fun, entertainment, conversation, gossip, and great company.
fun_fact: St. Patrick's Day on March 17 is celebrated in more countries across the world than any other national holiday.
short_desc: Emerald green landscapes, Cliffs of Moher, Guinness stout brewing, traditional fiddle music pub sessions, and literary heritage.

name: Israel
famous_for: Historic Old City of Jerusalem (Western Wall, Church of the Holy Sepulchre), Dead Sea buoyant waters, and Tel Aviv high-tech.
tourists: Over 4.5M visitors; famous for Jerusalem sacred sites, Bahá'í Gardens in Haifa, and Masada mountain fortress.
must_know: Shabbat begins every Friday at sunset and continues until Saturday night; public transport pauses and families gather for dinner.
fun_fact: The Dead Sea is the lowest point on the surface of the dry Earth, sitting at 430 meters below sea level with 34% salinity.
short_desc: Historic Old City of Jerusalem (Western Wall, Church of the Holy Sepulchre), Dead Sea buoyant waters, and Tel Aviv high-tech.

name: Italy
famous_for: The Colosseum, Venice romantic gondola canals, Florence Renaissance masterpieces, Pizza, Pasta, and haute couture fashion.
tourists: Over 64.5M international visitors annually (one of the top 5 worldwide); famous for Vatican Museums, Pompeii, and Amalfi Coast.
must_know: Never order a Cappuccino after 11:00 AM; Italians drink milk-based coffees strictly in the morning for proper digestion.
fun_fact: Italy contains 59 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, more than any other single country on the planet.
short_desc: The Colosseum, Venice romantic gondola canals, Florence Renaissance masterpieces, Pizza, Pasta, and haute couture fashion.

name: Ivory Coast
famous_for: World's largest cocoa producer, monumental Basilica of Yamoussoukro, and lively Zouglou music.
tourists: Over 2.0M visitors; highlights include Basilica of Our Lady of Peace and Taï National Park.
must_know: Abidjan is celebrated as the cultural and nightlife capital of West Africa ('Paris of West Africa').
fun_fact: The Basilica of Our Lady of Peace in Yamoussoukro is the largest Christian church building in the world.
short_desc: World's largest cocoa producer, monumental Basilica of Yamoussoukro, and lively Zouglou music.

name: Jamaica
famous_for: Birthplace of Reggae music (Bob Marley), Blue Mountain specialty coffee, fiery Jerk chicken, and Seven Mile Beach in Negril.
tourists: Over 4.1M tourists annually; famous for Dunn's River Falls, Bob Marley Museum, and Doctor's Cave Beach.
must_know: 'One Love' and 'No Problem, Mon' encapsulate the relaxed, welcoming, and deeply resilient Rastafarian-influenced spirit.
fun_fact: Jamaica was the first Caribbean nation to produce commercial rum and continues to make world-renowned pot-still rums.
short_desc: Birthplace of Reggae music (Bob Marley), Blue Mountain specialty coffee, fiery Jerk chicken, and Seven Mile Beach in Negril.

name: Japan
famous_for: Mount Fuji, ancient Kyoto shrines, bullet trains (Shinkansen), Anime, Shinto rituals, Sushi, and Hanami cherry blossoms.
tourists: Over 31.9M international tourists annually; famous for Fushimi Inari torii gates, Senso-ji, and Hiroshima Peace Park.
must_know: Bowing (Ojigi) is an essential sign of respect; tipping is not practiced and can be taken as insulting; remove shoes indoors.
fun_fact: Japan has over 5 million vending machines selling everything from hot canned coffee and umbrellas to fresh ramen.
short_desc: Mount Fuji, ancient Kyoto shrines, bullet trains (Shinkansen), Anime, Shinto rituals, Sushi, and Hanami cherry blossoms.

name: Jordan
famous_for: The rose-red rock city of Petra, Wadi Rum red desert canyon, buoyant Dead Sea, and ancient Roman Jerash.
tourists: Over 5.3M visitors; famous for The Treasury (Al-Khazneh) in Petra, Bedouin desert camps, and Mount Nebo.
must_know: Bedouin hospitality dictates offering guests three small cups of cardamom coffee: for the guest, for enjoyment, and for the sword.
fun_fact: Petra was carved directly into sandstone canyon cliffs by the Nabataean kingdom over 2,000 years ago.
short_desc: The rose-red rock city of Petra, Wadi Rum red desert canyon, buoyant Dead Sea, and ancient Roman Jerash.

name: Kazakhstan
famous_for: World's largest landlocked country, Baikonur Cosmodrome (space launch pad), Charyn Canyon, and nomadic horseback heritage.
tourists: Over 8.5M visitors; famous for Lake Kaindy sunken forest, Medeu high-altitude ice rink, and modern Astana architecture.
must_know: The dombra is a sacred two-stringed lute central to Kazakh musical storytelling; every household cherishes one.
fun_fact: Kazakhstan's Baikonur Cosmodrome was the launch site for both Sputnik 1 and Yuri Gagarin, the first human in space.
short_desc: World's largest landlocked country, Baikonur Cosmodrome (space launch pad), Charyn Canyon, and nomadic horseback heritage.

name: Kenya
famous_for: The Great Wildebeest Migration in Maasai Mara, Mount Kenya, red-robed Maasai warriors, and world-record marathon runners.
tourists: Over 2.0M safari visitors annually; famous for Amboseli elephant herds under Kilimanjaro and Lake Nakuru flamingos.
must_know: 'Hakuna Matata' is real Swahili meaning 'no troubles'; the communal concept of Harambee ('pulling together') unites communities.
fun_fact: Every year between July and October, over two million wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles brave crocodile-infested Mara River crossings.
short_desc: The Great Wildebeest Migration in Maasai Mara, Mount Kenya, red-robed Maasai warriors, and world-record marathon runners.

name: Kosovo
famous_for: Historic Ottoman stone bridges in Prizren, Rugova Canyon rock walls, medieval monasteries of Decani, and young coffee culture.
tourists: Approx. 350,000 visitors; famous for Sinan Pasha Mosque, Prizren Fortress overlooking river, and Mirusha waterfalls.
must_know: Kosovo has the youngest population in Europe, with over 50% of its residents under 30 years old, fueling vibrant cafe life.
fun_fact: The Newborn monument in Pristina is repainted with fresh artistic murals every year on Independence Day (February 17).
short_desc: Historic Ottoman stone bridges in Prizren, Rugova Canyon rock walls, medieval monasteries of Decani, and young coffee culture.

name: Kuwait
famous_for: Iconic mushroom-shaped Kuwait Towers, Sheikh Jaber Al-Ahmad Cultural Centre, pearl diving maritime past, and Grand Mosque.
tourists: Approx. 300,000 visitors; famous for Kuwait Towers, Souq Al-Mubarakiya historic bazaar, and Failaka Island archaeological ruins.
must_know: The Kuwaiti Dinar (KWD) is the single highest-valued currency unit in the entire world relative to the US Dollar.
fun_fact: The Diwaniya is a cherished social gathering hall where men meet in evenings to discuss politics, culture, and business over tea.
short_desc: Iconic mushroom-shaped Kuwait Towers, Sheikh Jaber Al-Ahmad Cultural Centre, pearl diving maritime past, and Grand Mosque.

name: Kyrgyzstan
famous_for: Tian Shan mountain range ('Celestial Mountains'), pristine alpine Lake Issyk-Kul, yurt dwelling nomad life, and eagle hunting.
tourists: Over 6.9M visitors; famous for Song-Kul horse riding treks, Ala Archa National Park, and Sulaiman-Too sacred mountain.
must_know: The traditional felt Yurt (Boz-ui) is so central to Kyrgyz identity that its wooden crown (Tunduk) appears on the national flag.
fun_fact: The Epic of Manas is one of the world's longest epic poems with over 500,000 poetic lines passed down orally by Manaschi bards.
short_desc: Tian Shan mountain range ('Celestial Mountains'), pristine alpine Lake Issyk-Kul, yurt dwelling nomad life, and eagle hunting.

name: Laos
famous_for: Luang Prabang UNESCO spiritual town, early morning saffron-robed monk almsgiving, Kuang Si turquoise falls, and 4,000 Islands.
tourists: Over 4.8M visitors; highlights include Wat Xieng Thong, Plain of Jars mysterious megaliths, and Mekong river cruises.
must_know: The early morning Tak Bat (Almsgiving ceremony) is a sacred silent ritual where locals offer sticky rice to passing monks.
fun_fact: Laos consumes more sticky rice (khao niao) per capita than any other nation in the world, eating it by hand from woven bamboo baskets.
short_desc: Luang Prabang UNESCO spiritual town, early morning saffron-robed monk almsgiving, Kuang Si turquoise falls, and 4,000 Islands.

name: Latvia
famous_for: Riga's world-class Art Nouveau architecture, UNESCO medieval cobblestone Old Town, Baltic amber, and nationwide Song festivals.
tourists: Over 1.8M tourists; famous for House of the Black Heads, Gauja National Park bobsleigh and castles, and Jūrmala sandy beaches.
must_know: Over one-third of the buildings in central Riga are built in the ornate Art Nouveau style, more than any other European capital.
fun_fact: Midsummer (Jāņi) on June 23-24 is Latvia's most cherished holiday, celebrated overnight around bonfires wearing oak-leaf and flower crowns.
short_desc: Riga's world-class Art Nouveau architecture, UNESCO medieval cobblestone Old Town, Baltic amber, and nationwide Song festivals.

name: Lebanon
famous_for: Roman temples of Baalbek, ancient Phoenician port of Byblos (oldest inhabited city), cedar trees, and gourmet mezze cuisine.
tourists: Over 1.9M tourists annually; famous for Jeita Grotto crystal caves, Pigeon Rocks in Raouche, and Byblos harbor.
must_know: The cedar tree (Cedrus libani) has been prized since biblical times and stands as the proud central emblem on Lebanon's flag.
fun_fact: Byblos in Lebanon is believed to have been continuously inhabited for over 7,000 years, and gave its name to the word 'Bible'.
short_desc: Roman temples of Baalbek, ancient Phoenician port of Byblos (oldest inhabited city), cedar trees, and gourmet mezze cuisine.

name: Lesotho
famous_for: 'Kingdom in the Sky' (only country entirely above 1,000m), Maletsunyane single-drop falls, and Basotho wool blankets.
tourists: Over 1.1M visitors; famous for Semonkong abseiling at Maletsunyane Falls, Sani Pass 4x4 trails, and Afriski slopes.
must_know: The Basotho woolen blanket (Kobo) and woven conical hat (Mokorotlo) are proud national garments worn in daily mountain life.
fun_fact: Lesotho has the highest lowest-point of any sovereign country in the world, with its lowest point sitting at 1,400 meters altitude.
short_desc: 'Kingdom in the Sky' (only country entirely above 1,000m), Maletsunyane single-drop falls, and Basotho wool blankets.

name: Liberia
famous_for: World-class surf breaks of Robertsport, Sapo National Park primary rainforest, pygmy hippos, and American-settler heritage.
tourists: Approx. 120,000 visitors; famous for Robertsport beaches, Providence Island, and Kpatawee Waterfalls.
must_know: Liberia is Africa's oldest modern republic, founded in 1847 by freed African Americans assisted by the American Colonization Society.
fun_fact: Sapo National Park contains the second-largest area of primary tropical rainforest in West Africa and shelters endangered pygmy hippos.
short_desc: World-class surf breaks of Robertsport, Sapo National Park primary rainforest, pygmy hippos, and American-settler heritage.

name: Libya
famous_for: Magnificent Roman ruins of Leptis Magna and Sabratha along the Mediterranean, and the Sahara desert oasis of Ghadames.
tourists: Approx. 95,000 visitors; known for Leptis Magna amphitheatre, Arch of Marcus Aurelius in Tripoli, and Akakus rock art.
must_know: Leptis Magna was one of the grandest cities of the Roman Empire, birthplace of Emperor Septimius Severus.
fun_fact: Ghadames, the 'Pearl of the Desert', is a UNESCO-inscribed mud-brick oasis town with whitewashed rooftop pedestrian alleys.
short_desc: Magnificent Roman ruins of Leptis Magna and Sabratha along the Mediterranean, and the Sahara desert oasis of Ghadames.

name: Lithuania
famous_for: Baroque Old Town of Vilnius, fairy-tale red-brick Trakai Island Castle on Lake Galvė, Curonian Spit dunes, and amber.
tourists: Over 2.9M visitors; famous for Hill of Crosses with over 100,000 crosses, Trakai Castle, and Republic of Užupis bohemian quarter.
must_know: Lithuanian is one of the oldest living Indo-European languages in the world, preserving ancient grammatical forms close to Sanskrit.
fun_fact: The Republic of Užupis in Vilnius is a whimsical artist enclave that declared itself an independent micronation with its own quirky constitution.
short_desc: Baroque Old Town of Vilnius, fairy-tale red-brick Trakai Island Castle on Lake Galvė, Curonian Spit dunes, and amber.

name: Luxembourg
famous_for: Bock Casemates subterranean fortress tunnels, fairytale Vianden Castle, Ardennes hills, and world-leading GDP per capita.
tourists: Over 1.2M visitors; famous for Luxembourg City Old Quarters, Chemin de la Corniche ('Europe's most beautiful balcony'), and Müllerthal trail.
must_know: Luxembourg was the first country in the world to make all public transport (trains, trams, and buses) entirely free nationwide.
fun_fact: Over 47% of Luxembourg's total resident population consists of foreign nationals representing over 170 diverse cultures.
short_desc: Bock Casemates subterranean fortress tunnels, fairytale Vianden Castle, Ardennes hills, and world-leading GDP per capita.

name: Madagascar
famous_for: Avenue of the Baobabs, lemurs found nowhere else on Earth, Tsingy de Bemaraha razor-sharp limestone karst, and vanilla beans.
tourists: Approx. 300,000 eco-tourists; famous for Avenue of the Baobabs, Andasibe-Mantadia rainforest lemurs, and Nosy Be coral beaches.
must_know: Over 90% of all wildlife in Madagascar is endemic, meaning it cannot be found naturally anywhere else on planet Earth.
fun_fact: Madagascar is the world's leading producer of Bourbon vanilla, hand-pollinated orchid pods prized by global pastry chefs.
short_desc: Avenue of the Baobabs, lemurs found nowhere else on Earth, Tsingy de Bemaraha razor-sharp limestone karst, and vanilla beans.

name: Malawi
famous_for: 'The Warm Heart of Africa' for friendly locals, crystal Lake Malawi with 1,000 cichlid fish species, and Mount Mulanje.
tourists: Approx. 1.0M visitors; famous for Lake Malawi snorkeling at Cape Maclear, Liwonde elephant safari, and Nyika plateau.
must_know: Lake Malawi National Park was the world's first freshwater national park and contains more species of fish than any other lake.
fun_fact: The Gule Wamkulu ritual masked dance of the Chewa people is recognized by UNESCO as Masterpiece of Oral and Intangible Heritage.
short_desc: 'The Warm Heart of Africa' for friendly locals, crystal Lake Malawi with 1,000 cichlid fish species, and Mount Mulanje.

name: Malaysia
famous_for: Petronas Twin Towers, Penang world-renowned street food, Mount Kinabalu in Borneo, ancient rainforests, and multicultural harmony.
tourists: Over 26.1M international visitors annually; famous for Batu Caves, Perhentian Islands coral reefs, and Langkawi cable car.
must_know: Never point with the forefinger; use the thumb of the right hand with the four fingers curled under as a respectful gesture.
fun_fact: The Taman Negara rainforest in peninsular Malaysia is estimated to be 130 million years old, older than the Amazon.
short_desc: Petronas Twin Towers, Penang world-renowned street food, Mount Kinabalu in Borneo, ancient rainforests, and multicultural harmony.

name: Mali
famous_for: Great Mosque of Djenné (world's largest mud-brick building), legendary desert outpost of Timbuktu, and Dogon cliff villages.
tourists: Approx. 160,000 visitors; famous for Great Mosque of Djenné, Bandiagara Escarpment, and Festival au Désert Tuareg music.
must_know: The annual replastering of the Great Mosque of Djenné (Crépissage) is a monumental community festival involving the entire town.
fun_fact: Mansa Musa, ruler of the medieval Mali Empire in the 14th century, is widely regarded by historians as the wealthiest human in history.
short_desc: Great Mosque of Djenné (world's largest mud-brick building), legendary desert outpost of Timbuktu, and Dogon cliff villages.

name: Malta
famous_for: Megalithic stone temples older than Stonehenge, walled fortress city of Valletta, Knights of St. John, and the Blue Lagoon in Comino.
tourists: Over 3.0M visitors; top attractions include St. John's Co-Cathedral (Caravaggio art), fortified silent city of Mdina, and Gozo citadel.
must_know: Maltese is the only Semitic language in the world that is written natively using the Latin alphabet.
fun_fact: Malta's megalithic temples, such as Ġgantija, were constructed around 3600 BC, making them older than the Great Pyramids of Giza.
short_desc: Megalithic stone temples older than Stonehenge, walled fortress city of Valletta, Knights of St. John, and the Blue Lagoon in Comino.

name: Mauritania
famous_for: Ancient desert caravan library town of Chinguetti, Richat Structure ('Eye of the Sahara'), and the iron ore desert train.
tourists: Approx. 15,000 heritage explorers; famous for Chinguetti ancient Quranic manuscripts and Banc d'Arguin migratory birds.
must_know: The iron ore train running from Zouérat to Nouadhibou is one of the longest and heaviest trains in the world, stretching over 2.5 kilometers.
fun_fact: The Richat Structure in western Mauritania is a prominent 40-kilometer circular geological dome visible from space.
short_desc: Ancient desert caravan library town of Chinguetti, Richat Structure ('Eye of the Sahara'), and the iron ore desert train.

name: Mexico
famous_for: Dia de los Muertos (Day of the Dead), Chichén Itzá Maya wonder, Mariachi music, Tacos, Tequila, and Frida Kahlo.
tourists: Over 42.2M international tourists annually (top 6 worldwide); famous for Riviera Maya, Teotihuacan pyramids, and colonial Oaxaca.
must_know: Mexican cuisine was awarded UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage status for preserving ancient corn, chili, and bean culinary heritage.
fun_fact: The Great Pyramid of Cholula in Puebla, Mexico is the largest archaeological pyramid monument by volume in the entire world.
short_desc: Dia de los Muertos (Day of the Dead), Chichén Itzá Maya wonder, Mariachi music, Tacos, Tequila, and Frida Kahlo.

name: Moldova
famous_for: Mileștii Mici underground wine cellars (world's largest wine collection in Guinness records), and Orheiul Vechi cliff monastery.
tourists: Approx. 180,000 visitors; famous for Cricova underground wine city, Orheiul Vechi cave churches, and Purcari vineyards.
must_know: Mileștii Mici holds nearly 2 million bottles of wine stored inside 200 kilometers of subterranean limestone excavation tunnels.
fun_fact: National Wine Day in early October transforms central Chișinău into an open-air celebration of historic winemaking traditions.
short_desc: Mileștii Mici underground wine cellars (world's largest wine collection in Guinness records), and Orheiul Vechi cliff monastery.

name: Mongolia
famous_for: Genghis Khan equestrian heritage, nomadic ger tents, Gobi Desert sand dunes, eagle hunters, and Naadam sports festival.
tourists: Over 650,000 visitors; famous for Gorkhi-Terelj National Park, Flaming Cliffs dinosaur fossils, and Lake Khövsgöl.
must_know: Hospitality is mandatory on the steppe: nomadic families keep their ger doors unlocked with hot milk tea waiting for travelers.
fun_fact: Mongolia is the most sparsely populated sovereign country in the world, with roughly 2 people per square kilometer.
short_desc: Genghis Khan equestrian heritage, nomadic ger tents, Gobi Desert sand dunes, eagle hunters, and Naadam sports festival.

name: Montenegro
famous_for: Fjord-like Bay of Kotor, dramatic cliffside Ostrog Monastery, Tara River Canyon (deepest in Europe), and Sveti Stefan island.
tourists: Over 2.6M visitors; highlights include Kotor Old Town, Durmitor National Park alpine lakes, and Budva medieval beaches.
must_know: Montenegro translates literally to 'Black Mountain', named for the dark, dense pine forests covering Mount Lovćen.
fun_fact: The Tara River Canyon plunges up to 1,300 meters (4,265 ft) deep, making it the deepest river canyon in all of Europe.
short_desc: Fjord-like Bay of Kotor, dramatic cliffside Ostrog Monastery, Tara River Canyon (deepest in Europe), and Sveti Stefan island.

name: Morocco
famous_for: Jemaa el-Fnaa square in Marrakech, blue-washed streets of Chefchaouen, Sahara sand dunes of Merzouga, and aromatic Tagines.
tourists: Over 14.5M international visitors annually; famous for Medina of Fez (oldest university), Hassan II Mosque, and Atlas mountains.
must_know: Moroccan mint tea is served poured from high above the glass to create a foamy crown, known with affection as 'Berber whiskey'.
fun_fact: The University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, founded in 859 AD by Fatima al-Fihri, is the oldest operating university in the world.
short_desc: Jemaa el-Fnaa square in Marrakech, blue-washed streets of Chefchaouen, Sahara sand dunes of Merzouga, and aromatic Tagines.

name: Mozambique
famous_for: Bazaruto Archipelago marine reserve (dolphins & dugongs), colonial Ilha de Moçambique, peri-peri prawns, and Marrabenta music.
tourists: Over 1.5M visitors; famous for Bazaruto sand dunes, Tofo whale shark diving, and Gorongosa National Park wildlife revival.
must_know: Ilha de Moçambique was a major Portuguese trading hub on the spice route for 400 years and holds the oldest European building in the south hemisphere.
fun_fact: The marine waters of Bazaruto Archipelago protect the last viable population of endangered dugongs in the Western Indian Ocean.
short_desc: Bazaruto Archipelago marine reserve (dolphins & dugongs), colonial Ilha de Moçambique, peri-peri prawns, and Marrabenta music.

name: Myanmar
famous_for: Over 2,000 ancient Buddhist temples across the plains of Bagan, gold-leaf Shwedagon Pagoda, and leg-rowing Inle Lake fishermen.
tourists: Approx. 1.8M visitors; famous for Bagan sunrise hot-air balloons, Shwedagon Pagoda in Yangon, and U Bein teak bridge.
must_know: Thanaka, a natural yellowish-white cosmetic paste made from ground bark, is worn on the faces of women and children for sun protection.
fun_fact: The Shwedagon Pagoda in Yangon is plated with thousands of genuine gold bars and its pinnacle is crowned with 5,448 diamonds.
short_desc: Over 2,000 ancient Buddhist temples across the plains of Bagan, gold-leaf Shwedagon Pagoda, and leg-rowing Inle Lake fishermen.

name: Namibia
famous_for: Towering red sand dunes of Sossusvlei, dead camelthorn trees of Deadvlei, Skeleton Coast shipwrecks, and Etosha pan wildlife.
tourists: Over 1.6M visitors; famous for Dune 45, Sossusvlei salt pan, Etosha waterholes, and Fish River Canyon.
must_know: Namibia was the first country in Africa to incorporate comprehensive environmental protection directly into its national constitution.
fun_fact: The Namib Desert is considered the oldest desert in the world, with arid conditions persisting for over 55 million years.
short_desc: Towering red sand dunes of Sossusvlei, dead camelthorn trees of Deadvlei, Skeleton Coast shipwrecks, and Etosha pan wildlife.

name: Nepal
famous_for: Mount Everest (Sagarmatha, 8,848m), Annapurna circuit trekking, birthplace of the Buddha in Lumbini, and Sherpa mountaineering.
tourists: Over 1.0M international trekking visitors; famous for Everest Base Camp, Kathmandu Durbar Square, and serene Phewa Lake.
must_know: Namaste with pressed palms is accompanied by a slight bow; always walk clockwise around Buddhist stupas and mani stones.
fun_fact: Nepal's national flag is the only non-quadrilateral flag in the world, formed of two stacked crimson triangular pennants.
short_desc: Mount Everest (Sagarmatha, 8,848m), Annapurna circuit trekking, birthplace of the Buddha in Lumbini, and Sherpa mountaineering.

name: Netherlands
famous_for: Amsterdam UNESCO canal rings, Keukenhof tulip gardens, historic windmills of Kinderdijk, bicycle paths, and Rembrandt art.
tourists: Over 20.3M international tourists annually; famous for Van Gogh Museum, Anne Frank House, and Rijksmuseum.
must_know: Directness is considered honest and respectful, not rude; bicycles always have the right of way on dedicated bike paths.
fun_fact: Roughly one-third of the Netherlands lies below sea level, protected by the Delta Works engineering marvel.
short_desc: Amsterdam UNESCO canal rings, Keukenhof tulip gardens, historic windmills of Kinderdijk, bicycle paths, and Rembrandt art.

name: New Caledonia
famous_for: World's largest enclosed coral lagoon, Isle of Pines ('Closest island to Paradise'), Kanak cultural totem woodcarvings, and nickel.
tourists: Over 130,000 visitors; famous for Heart of Voh mangrove formation, Isle of Pines turquoise bays, and Tjibaou Cultural Centre.
must_know: The Kanak custom of 'La Coutume' involves presenting a gift (cloth, money, or tobacco) to clan elders when entering tribal lands.
fun_fact: The New Caledonia Barrier Reef is the second-longest double barrier reef on Earth after the Belize Barrier Reef.
short_desc: World's largest enclosed coral lagoon, Isle of Pines ('Closest island to Paradise'), Kanak cultural totem woodcarvings, and nickel.

name: New Zealand
famous_for: Lord of the Rings dramatic landscapes, Milford Sound fiord, Māori Haka war dance, Queenstown adventure sports, and Kiwi bird.
tourists: Over 3.8M visitors annually; famous for Hobbiton movie set, Rotorua geothermal geysers, Tongariro Crossing, and Franz Josef glacier.
must_know: The Hongi is the traditional Māori greeting where two people press noses and foreheads together, sharing the breath of life (ha).
fun_fact: Queenstown, nestled on Lake Wakatipu, is universally acclaimed as the 'Adventure Capital of the World', home to the first commercial bungy jump.
short_desc: Lord of the Rings dramatic landscapes, Milford Sound fiord, Māori Haka war dance, Queenstown adventure sports, and Kiwi bird.

name: Nicaragua
famous_for: Volcano boarding down black cinder slopes of Cerro Negro, colonial pastel Granada on Lake Nicaragua, and Ometepe twin-volcano island.
tourists: Over 1.2M visitors; highlights include Granada cobblestones, Masaya glowing lava lake, and surf breaks in San Juan del Sur.
must_know: Lake Nicaragua is the largest freshwater lake in Central America and is uniquely home to oceanic bull sharks that swim upriver.
fun_fact: Cerro Negro is the only place in the world where thrill-seekers hike up an active volcano and sandboard down loose black ash at 80 km/h.
short_desc: Volcano boarding down black cinder slopes of Cerro Negro, colonial pastel Granada on Lake Nicaragua, and Ometepe twin-volcano island.

name: Niger
famous_for: Historic mud-brick Grand Mosque of Agadez (UNESCO gate to the Sahara), W National Park wildlife, and Wodaabe Gerewol dance.
tourists: Approx. 150,000 visitors; famous for Agadez clay minaret, Aïr Mountains rock art, and West African giraffe sanctuaries in Kouré.
must_know: The Gerewol festival is an ancient male beauty pageant where young Wodaabe men wear face paint and perform singing dances.
fun_fact: The Grand Mosque of Agadez is the tallest mud-brick structure in the world, standing 27 meters high since 1515.
short_desc: Historic mud-brick Grand Mosque of Agadez (UNESCO gate to the Sahara), W National Park wildlife, and Wodaabe Gerewol dance.

name: Nigeria
famous_for: Nollywood cinema industry (second in world by output), Afrobeats global music explosion (Burna Boy, Wizkid), and rich cultural empires.
tourists: Over 1.5M international visitors; famous for Lekki Conservation Centre, Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove, and Zuma Rock monolith.
must_know: Respecting elders is paramount; greetings frequently involve slight bowing or kneeling in Yoruba and Igbo customs.
fun_fact: Nigeria is Africa's most populous nation, home to more than 250 distinct ethnic groups speaking over 500 languages.
short_desc: Nollywood cinema industry (second in world by output), Afrobeats global music explosion (Burna Boy, Wizkid), and rich cultural empires.

name: North Korea
famous_for: Massive monument architecture in Pyongyang, Kumsusan Palace of the Sun, Mount Paektu sacred volcanic crater, and Arirang Games.
tourists: Approx. 100,000 visitors (strictly regulated group state tours); famous for Juche Tower, DMZ border crossing, and Kaesong ancient gates.
must_know: Bow respectfully before statues and portraits of state founders; all tourist activities are accompanied by official national guides.
fun_fact: The Ryugyong Hotel in Pyongyang is a colossal 105-story pyramid-shaped skyscraper that dominates the skyline.
short_desc: Massive monument architecture in Pyongyang, Kumsusan Palace of the Sun, Mount Paektu sacred volcanic crater, and Arirang Games.

name: North Macedonia
famous_for: Ancient crystalline Lake Ohrid (one of Europe's oldest lakes), historic monasteries, Ottoman Old Bazaar, and statue-filled Skopje.
tourists: Over 1.2M visitors; highlights include Church of St. John at Kaneo, Lake Ohrid boat rides, and Matka Canyon kayaking.
must_know: Lake Ohrid preserves a unique aquatic ecosystem with more than 200 endemic species that evolved over millions of years.
fun_fact: Mother Teresa (Saint Teresa of Calcutta) was born in Skopje in 1910 and spent the first 18 years of her life in the city.
short_desc: Ancient crystalline Lake Ohrid (one of Europe's oldest lakes), historic monasteries, Ottoman Old Bazaar, and statue-filled Skopje.

name: Northern Cyprus
famous_for: Kyrenia Castle harbor, Bellapais Abbey, ghost city of Varosha, and wild Karpaz donkeys.
tourists: Over 1.5M visitors; top sights include Kyrenia Harbour, St. Hilarion fairy-tale castle, and Salamis ruins.
must_know: Nicosia is the last divided capital in Europe, separated by a UN buffer zone with pedestrian border gates.
fun_fact: St. Hilarion Castle in the Kyrenia range is said to have inspired Walt Disney's Snow White castle.
short_desc: Kyrenia Castle harbor, Bellapais Abbey, ghost city of Varosha, and wild Karpaz donkeys.

name: Norway
famous_for: Geirangerfjord & Nærøyfjord dramatic sea fjords, Midnight Sun, Lofoten Islands fishing cabins, and Viking maritime history.
tourists: Over 5.9M international tourists annually; famous for Trolltunga cliff ledge, Preikestolen, Flåm Railway, and Tromsø aurora tours.
must_know: 'Allemannsretten' (Right to Roam) is a foundational law granting everyone freedom to hike and camp responsibly anywhere in nature.
fun_fact: Norway has the second-longest coastline in the world (over 100,000 km including fjords and islands) and introduced salmon sushi to Japan.
short_desc: Geirangerfjord & Nærøyfjord dramatic sea fjords, Midnight Sun, Lofoten Islands fishing cabins, and Viking maritime history.

name: Oman
famous_for: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque, frankincense tree groves in Dhofar, Bimmah Sinkhole, ancient Nizwa fort, and emerald wadis.
tourists: Over 3.2M tourists annually; famous for Wahiba Sands desert, Wadi Shab turquoise pools, and green Khareef monsoon in Salalah.
must_know: Frankincense resin has been harvested in Dhofar for over 5,000 years, once traded like gold to Pharaohs and Roman Emperors.
fun_fact: Oman is one of the oldest independent states in the Arab world, maintaining ancient dhow wooden shipbuilding traditions in Sur.
short_desc: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque, frankincense tree groves in Dhofar, Bimmah Sinkhole, ancient Nizwa fort, and emerald wadis.

name: Pakistan
famous_for: K2 mountain (world's second-highest, 8,611m), Hunza Valley, Mughal Badshahi Mosque in Lahore, truck art, and spicy Biryani.
tourists: Over 1.9M international visitors; highlights include Karakoram Highway ('Eighth Wonder'), Fairy Meadows, and Mohenjo-daro ruins.
must_know: Pakistani truck art transforms commercial cargo trucks into moving kaleidoscopic masterpieces of floral calligraphy and mirrors.
fun_fact: The Karakoram Highway links Pakistan to China through the Khunjerab Pass at 4,693m, the highest paved international border crossing.
short_desc: K2 mountain (world's second-highest, 8,611m), Hunza Valley, Mughal Badshahi Mosque in Lahore, truck art, and spicy Biryani.

name: Palestine
famous_for: Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem, ancient city of Jericho (oldest walled city on Earth), olive tree groves, embroidery, and Knafeh.
tourists: Approx. 1.0M pilgrims and visitors (historical); famous for Church of the Nativity, Old City of Hebron, and Mar Saba monastery.
must_know: The ancient olive harvest season in October is a cherished family festival where extended families gather to pick olives and press extra virgin oil.
fun_fact: Jericho is widely recognized as one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on Earth, with archaeological ruins dating back over 11,000 years.
short_desc: Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem, ancient city of Jericho (oldest walled city on Earth), olive tree groves, embroidery, and Knafeh.

name: Panama
famous_for: The Panama Canal (engineering marvel of the 20th century), Bocas del Toro coral archipelago, and San Blas Kuna Yala islands.
tourists: Over 2.5M visitors; famous for Miraflores Locks canal transit, Casco Viejo colonial district, and Boquete mountain coffee.
must_know: The Panama Hat actually originated in Ecuador, but acquired its worldwide name because American workers wore them during canal construction.
fun_fact: Panama is the only place on Earth where one can watch the sun rise over the Pacific Ocean and set over the Atlantic Ocean from Mount Volcán Barú.
short_desc: The Panama Canal (engineering marvel of the 20th century), Bocas del Toro coral archipelago, and San Blas Kuna Yala islands.

name: Papua New Guinea
famous_for: Over 850 living indigenous languages, Birds-of-Paradise feathers, vibrant Highland Sing-Sing tribal gatherings, and Kokoda Track.
tourists: Approx. 200,000 eco-explorers; famous for Mount Hagen Cultural Show, Goroka Show, and Sepik River crocodile woodcarvings.
must_know: Papua New Guinea is the most linguistically diverse place on Earth, accounting for roughly 12% of all languages spoken by humankind.
fun_fact: Over 30 species of Birds-of-Paradise inhabit the mountain rainforests, famous for surreal courtship dances and iridescent plumage.
short_desc: Over 850 living indigenous languages, Birds-of-Paradise feathers, vibrant Highland Sing-Sing tribal gatherings, and Kokoda Track.

name: Paraguay
famous_for: Tereré cold yerba mate drinking culture, Itaipu hydroelectric dam (one of the largest on Earth), and UNESCO Jesuit Missions.
tourists: Over 1.2M visitors; famous for Jesuit Missions of La Santísima Trinidad, Saltos del Monday waterfalls, and Gran Chaco wilderness.
