must_know: Tereré—drinking cold-brewed yerba mate with medicinal herbs (yuyos) from a guampa horn—is UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.
fun_fact: Guaraní is spoken by over 90% of the population, making Paraguay one of the only Latin American countries where an indigenous tongue is dominant.
short_desc: Tereré cold yerba mate drinking culture, Itaipu hydroelectric dam (one of the largest on Earth), and UNESCO Jesuit Missions.

name: Peru
famous_for: Machu Picchu Incan citadel, Rainbow Mountain (Vinicunca), Nazca desert geoglyphs, ceviche culinary capital, and Sacred Valley.
tourists: Over 4.4M international visitors; famous for Inca Trail trek, Lake Titicaca floating reed islands, and Colca Canyon condors.
must_know: Greeting with a light kiss on the right cheek is standard; Peruvians take immense pride in Lima being South America's gastronomic hub.
fun_fact: Peru is the birthplace of the potato, cultivating more than 4,000 native varieties ranging in purple, yellow, and red hues.
short_desc: Machu Picchu Incan citadel, Rainbow Mountain (Vinicunca), Nazca desert geoglyphs, ceviche culinary capital, and Sacred Valley.

name: Philippines
famous_for: Over 7,000 tropical islands, white sands of Boracay, limestone lagoons of El Nido Palawan, Banaue Rice Terraces, and Jeepneys.
tourists: Over 8.2M international tourists; famous for Chocolate Hills in Bohol, Puerto Princesa Underground River, and whale sharks.
must_know: 'Bayanihan' is the spirit of communal unity, traditionally depicted as neighbors physically lifting and carrying a bamboo hut together.
fun_fact: The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan flows 8.2 kilometers through a massive limestone cave directly into the sea.
short_desc: Over 7,000 tropical islands, white sands of Boracay, limestone lagoons of El Nido Palawan, Banaue Rice Terraces, and Jeepneys.

name: Poland
famous_for: Historic UNESCO Kraków Old Town, Wieliczka subterranean Salt Mine, Białowieża primeval forest, Chopin piano music, and Pierogi.
tourists: Over 21.0M international tourists; famous for Wawel Royal Castle, Malbork brick fortress, and Tatra mountain ski trails.
must_know: Guests are welcomed with bread and salt; it is customary to remove shoes upon entering someone's home and put on offered slippers.
fun_fact: Wieliczka Salt Mine near Kraków features entire underground chapels, chandeliers, and statues carved entirely out of rock salt.
short_desc: Historic UNESCO Kraków Old Town, Wieliczka subterranean Salt Mine, Białowieża primeval forest, Chopin piano music, and Pierogi.

name: Portugal
famous_for: Pastéis de Nata custard tarts, nostalgic Fado acoustic music, Douro Valley port wine terraced hills, and yellow Tram 28 in Lisbon.
tourists: Over 26.5M international visitors annually; famous for Pena Palace in Sintra, Belém Tower, and Algarve golden sea caves.
must_know: Fado music is an emotional Portuguese art form expressing 'Saudade'—a profound melancholic longing for something lost.
fun_fact: Portugal is the world's leading producer of natural cork, harvesting over 50% of the globe's total cork bark supply.
short_desc: Pastéis de Nata custard tarts, nostalgic Fado acoustic music, Douro Valley port wine terraced hills, and yellow Tram 28 in Lisbon.

name: Puerto Rico
famous_for: Historic Old San Juan cobblestones, El Yunque National Forest (only US tropical rainforest), bioluminescent bays, and Salsa music.
tourists: Over 5.0M visitors; famous for Castillo San Felipe del Morro, Flamenco Beach in Culebra, and Mosquito Bioluminescent Bay.
must_know: Puerto Rico is the birthplace of the Piña Colada cocktail, created in Old San Juan in the 1950s.
fun_fact: Mosquito Bay on Vieques island is recognized by Guinness as the brightest bioluminescent bay on Earth, illuminated by dinoflagellates.
short_desc: Historic Old San Juan cobblestones, El Yunque National Forest (only US tropical rainforest), bioluminescent bays, and Salsa music.

name: Qatar
famous_for: Museum of Islamic Art designed by I.M. Pei, Katara Cultural Village, Souq Waqif falcon market, and 2022 FIFA World Cup host.
tourists: Over 4.0M visitors; famous for Doha Corniche, inland desert sea of Khor Al Adaid, and futuristic Lusail skyline.
must_know: Greet hosts with a respectful handshake; respect Islamic traditions by dressing conservatively in public malls and cultural centers.
fun_fact: Khor Al Adaid in southern Qatar is one of the only places on Earth where deep sea water floods into the heart of tall desert sand dunes.
short_desc: Museum of Islamic Art designed by I.M. Pei, Katara Cultural Village, Souq Waqif falcon market, and 2022 FIFA World Cup host.

name: Republic of the Congo
famous_for: Odzala-Kokoua National Park, western lowland gorillas, Congo River rapids, and La Sape dandy culture.
tourists: Approx. 180,000 visitors; known for Odzala gorilla treks, Loufoulakari Falls, and Pointe-Noire beaches.
must_know: Brazzaville sits right across the river from Kinshasa, the two closest national capitals after Rome/Vatican.
fun_fact: The Congo River is the deepest recorded river in the world, with depths plunging beyond 220 meters.
short_desc: Odzala-Kokoua National Park, western lowland gorillas, Congo River rapids, and La Sape dandy culture.

name: Romania
famous_for: Transylvanian Bran Castle (associated with Dracula), painted monasteries of Bucovina, Transfăgărășan alpine highway, and Danube Delta.
tourists: Over 13.6M visitors; famous for Peleș Castle, medieval Sighișoara (birthplace of Vlad the Impaler), and Palace of the Parliament.
must_know: The Palace of the Parliament in Bucharest is the heaviest administrative building on Earth, constructed with 700,000 tonnes of steel.
fun_fact: Top Gear dubbed Romania's winding Transfăgărășan highway through the Carpathian Mountains as 'the best driving road in the world'.
short_desc: Transylvanian Bran Castle (associated with Dracula), painted monasteries of Bucovina, Transfăgărășan alpine highway, and Danube Delta.

name: Russia
famous_for: Red Square & Saint Basil's onion domes, Hermitage Museum, Trans-Siberian railway, Lake Baikal (deepest on Earth), and Ballet.
tourists: Over 24.4M visitors (historical peak); famous for Moscow Kremlin, Peterhof fountain cascades, and Lake Baikal crystal blue ice.
must_know: Never shake hands across a doorway threshold, as Russian folklore holds this causes bitter arguments and bad fortune.
fun_fact: Lake Baikal holds roughly 20% of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water, more than all five North American Great Lakes combined.
short_desc: Red Square & Saint Basil's onion domes, Hermitage Museum, Trans-Siberian railway, Lake Baikal (deepest on Earth), and Ballet.

name: Rwanda
famous_for: 'Land of a Thousand Hills', mountain gorilla tracking in Volcanoes National Park, spotless green Kigali, and Umuganda community service.
tourists: Over 1.2M eco-tourists; famous for Volcanoes gorilla treks, Nyungwe canopy walkway, and Akagera Big Five safari.
must_know: On the last Saturday morning of every month, all citizens take part in 'Umuganda', a mandatory nationwide community clean-up day.
fun_fact: Rwanda has the highest percentage of female parliamentarians in the world, with women holding over 60% of legislative seats.
short_desc: 'Land of a Thousand Hills', mountain gorilla tracking in Volcanoes National Park, spotless green Kigali, and Umuganda community service.

name: Saudi Arabia
famous_for: Sacred holy cities of Mecca and Medina, ancient Nabataean rock tombs of Hegra in AlUla, vast Rub' al Khali desert, and Arabian horses.
tourists: Over 18.0M visitors; famous for AlUla Hegra tombs, historic Al-Balad district in Jeddah, and Edge of the World cliffs in Riyadh.
must_know: Hospitality is legendary; offering Arabic coffee (Gahwa) flavored with cardamom and sweet dates is the quintessential welcome.
fun_fact: The Rub' al Khali (Empty Quarter) desert in southern Saudi Arabia is the largest continuous sand desert on planet Earth.
short_desc: Sacred holy cities of Mecca and Medina, ancient Nabataean rock tombs of Hegra in AlUla, vast Rub' al Khali desert, and Arabian horses.

name: Senegal
famous_for: 'Teranga' (world-famous Senegalese hospitality), pink Lake Retba, colonial Saint-Louis jazz, Gorée Island, and Sabar drumming.
tourists: Over 1.7M visitors; famous for House of Slaves on Gorée Island, African Renaissance Monument, and surfing in Dakar.
must_know: 'Teranga' is the national philosophy of hospitality, respect, and community generosity that welcomes all strangers as family.
fun_fact: Lake Retba (Lac Rose) north of Dakar turns vivid pink due to salt-loving Dunaliella salina algae and holds 40% salinity.
short_desc: 'Teranga' (world-famous Senegalese hospitality), pink Lake Retba, colonial Saint-Louis jazz, Gorée Island, and Sabar drumming.

name: Serbia
famous_for: Belgrade Fortress (Kalemegdan) at confluence of Danube and Sava, EXIT music festival in Petrovaradin, and Tara National Park.
tourists: Over 3.8M visitors; famous for Saint Sava Temple, skull tower of Niš, Uvac river canyon meanders, and Guča trumpet festival.
must_know: 'Slava' is a unique Serbian Orthodox family celebration honoring the family's patron saint with feast food, wine, and slavski kolač bread.
fun_fact: Belgrade is one of the oldest cities in Europe, having been destroyed and rebuilt over 40 times throughout its storied history.
short_desc: Belgrade Fortress (Kalemegdan) at confluence of Danube and Sava, EXIT music festival in Petrovaradin, and Tara National Park.

name: Sierra Leone
famous_for: Untouched white sand beaches of the Freetown Peninsula (River No. 2 Beach), Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary, and Krio culture.
tourists: Approx. 110,000 visitors; famous for River Number Two Beach, Bunce Island slave castle ruins, and Outamba-Kilimi National Park.
must_know: The historic Cotton Tree in central Freetown stood as a symbol of freedom for freed enslaved settlers arriving in 1792.
fun_fact: Sierra Leone's coast features some of the finest undeveloped powder-white beaches in Africa, fringed by lush green rainforest hills.
short_desc: Untouched white sand beaches of the Freetown Peninsula (River No. 2 Beach), Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary, and Krio culture.

name: Slovakia
famous_for: High Tatras alpine peaks, Spiš Castle (one of central Europe's largest castle ruins), and over 6,000 natural karst caves.
tourists: Over 5.0M visitors; famous for Bojnice fairytale castle, Dobšinská Ice Cave, and Bratislava Old Town cobblestones.
must_know: Slovakia possesses the highest concentration of castles and fortified ruins per capita in the world, with over 180 castles and 425 châteaux.
fun_fact: Dobšinská Ice Cave in Slovak Paradise is an underground wonder where glacier ice fills colossal limestone caverns year-round.
short_desc: High Tatras alpine peaks, Spiš Castle (one of central Europe's largest castle ruins), and over 6,000 natural karst caves.

name: Slovenia
famous_for: Emerald Lake Bled with church island, Postojna Cave subterranean train, Julian Alps, and green dragon capital of Ljubljana.
tourists: Over 6.2M international tourists; famous for Lake Bled pletna boat rides, Lake Bohinj, and emerald Soča River white-water rafting.
must_know: Over 60% of Slovenia is blanketed in lush forest; it was declared the world's first certified Green Destination country.
fun_fact: Lake Bled features a tiny teardrop-shaped island; local tradition requires grooms to carry their brides up all 99 stone steps.
short_desc: Emerald Lake Bled with church island, Postojna Cave subterranean train, Julian Alps, and green dragon capital of Ljubljana.

name: Solomon Islands
famous_for: World-renowned WWII Guadalcanal shipwreck diving, Marovo Lagoon (world's largest double barrier lagoon), and shell money.
tourists: Approx. 30,000 scuba divers and explorers; famous for Iron Bottom Sound dive wrecks and Marovo wood carvings.
must_know: Traditional shell money (Tafuliae) made of polished seashell discs is still used for ceremonial bride-price and land compensations.
fun_fact: Marovo Lagoon is framed by volcanic islands and coral atolls, praised by author James Michener as the eighth wonder of the world.
short_desc: World-renowned WWII Guadalcanal shipwreck diving, Marovo Lagoon (world's largest double barrier lagoon), and shell money.

name: Somalia
famous_for: Longest coastline in mainland Africa, historic Mogadishu stone architecture, frankincense production, and 'Nation of Poets' heritage.
tourists: Approx. 50,000 visitors (mostly diaspora and business); famous for Mogadishu Lido beach and Puntland frankincense groves.
must_know: Somalia is celebrated throughout the Arab and African worlds as the 'Nation of Poets' because oral poetry holds immense social power.
fun_fact: Somalia possesses over 3,330 kilometers of unbroken Indian Ocean and Gulf of Aden coastline, the longest on mainland Africa.
short_desc: Longest coastline in mainland Africa, historic Mogadishu stone architecture, frankincense production, and 'Nation of Poets' heritage.

name: Somaliland
famous_for: Laas Geel prehistoric rock art (among Africa's best preserved cave paintings), camel market in Hargeisa, and historic Berbera port.
tourists: Approx. 20,000 heritage travelers; famous for 5,000-year-old colorful bovine rock paintings of Laas Geel and Daallo mountain forest.
must_know: The camel is deeply revered in Somaliland, serving as a pillar of nomadic wealth, milk production, and oral poetic lore.
fun_fact: The cave paintings at Laas Geel date back between 5,000 and 11,000 years and retain strikingly vibrant red, white, and yellow pigments.
short_desc: Laas Geel prehistoric rock art (among Africa's best preserved cave paintings), camel market in Hargeisa, and historic Berbera port.

name: South Africa
famous_for: Table Mountain, Kruger National Park Big Five safari, Cape of Good Hope, Nelson Mandela legacy, and Cape Winelands.
tourists: Over 10.2M international tourists annually; famous for Table Mountain cableway, Boulders Beach penguins, and Robben Island.
must_know: A 'Braai' (barbecue over wood embers) is the supreme national cultural pastime bringing South Africans of all backgrounds together.
fun_fact: South Africa has three official capital cities: Pretoria (Executive), Cape Town (Legislative), and Bloemfontein (Judicial).
short_desc: Table Mountain, Kruger National Park Big Five safari, Cape of Good Hope, Nelson Mandela legacy, and Cape Winelands.

name: South Korea
famous_for: K-Pop (BTS, Blackpink), K-Dramas, Samsung high-tech innovation, Kimchi, Hanok heritage villages, and Korean BBQ.
tourists: Over 17.5M tourists annually; famous for Gyeongbokgung Palace, Bukchon Hanok Village, Jeju volcanic waterfalls, and Myeongdong.
must_know: Bowing is customary; always use both hands when pouring drinks or handing payment to an elder as a deep sign of respect.
fun_fact: South Korea has the world's fastest average internet speeds and was the first country to deploy commercial 5G mobile networks nationwide.
short_desc: K-Pop (BTS, Blackpink), K-Dramas, Samsung high-tech innovation, Kimchi, Hanok heritage villages, and Korean BBQ.

name: South Sudan
famous_for: World's newest sovereign nation (independent since 2011), vast Sudd wetland marsh, and traditional Dinka and Nuer cattle culture.
tourists: Approx. 25,000 visitors; famous for Boma-Jonglei annual wildlife migration and the vast Nile Sudd papyrus swamps.
must_know: Cattle are regarded as the ultimate symbol of wealth, status, and community bonding in traditional pastoralist life.
fun_fact: The Sudd is one of the largest freshwater wetland ecosystems in the world, spanning over 30,000 square kilometers.
short_desc: World's newest sovereign nation (independent since 2011), vast Sudd wetland marsh, and traditional Dinka and Nuer cattle culture.

name: Spain
famous_for: Sagrada Família, Flamenco passionate dance, Paella, Tapas culture, Alhambra palace, and sunny beaches.
tourists: Over 85.1M international tourists annually (second in the world); famous for Park Güell, Prado Museum, and Ibiza.
must_know: Afternoon siesta culture and very late dining (dinners at 9:30-11:00 PM) are cherished social norms.
fun_fact: Spain is home to the world's oldest continuously operating restaurant: Sobrino de Botín in Madrid, opened in 1725.
short_desc: Sagrada Família, Flamenco passionate dance, Paella, Tapas culture, Alhambra palace, and sunny beaches.

name: Sri Lanka
famous_for: Sigiriya rock fortress ('Lion Rock'), Ceylon black tea plantations, blue whales of Mirissa, and scenic Kandy-to-Ella train ride.
tourists: Over 1.5M international visitors; famous for Sigiriya, Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic, Yala leopard safari, and Galle Fort.
must_know: A gentle side-to-side head wobble in Sri Lanka is a warm, affirmative gesture conveying 'yes', understanding, and agreement.
fun_fact: Sri Lanka was the first nation in modern world history to elect a female Prime Minister: Sirimavo Bandaranaike in 1960.
short_desc: Sigiriya rock fortress ('Lion Rock'), Ceylon black tea plantations, blue whales of Mirissa, and scenic Kandy-to-Ella train ride.

name: Sudan
famous_for: Over 200 Nubian pyramids of Meroë (more pyramids than Egypt!), confluence of the Blue and White Niles, and Sufi whirling dervishes.
tourists: Approx. 80,000 heritage explorers; famous for Pyramids of Meroë, temple of Soleb, and Red Sea coral reefs at Sanganeb.
must_know: Sudan is home to roughly 255 ancient pyramids built by the Kingdom of Kush, far outnumbering Egypt's total pyramid count.
fun_fact: At Khartoum, the sediment-rich Blue Nile from Ethiopia unites with the tranquil White Nile from Uganda to form the main Nile River.
short_desc: Over 200 Nubian pyramids of Meroë (more pyramids than Egypt!), confluence of the Blue and White Niles, and Sufi whirling dervishes.

name: Suriname
famous_for: UNESCO Dutch wooden architecture of Paramaribo, Central Suriname Nature Reserve rainforest, and harmonious multicultural harmony.
tourists: Over 300,000 visitors; famous for Saint Peter and Paul Wooden Cathedral, Brownsberg rainforest park, and sea turtle nesting at Galibi.
must_know: In downtown Paramaribo, the Neveh Shalom Synagogue and the Keizerstraat Mosque sit peacefully right next door to each other.
fun_fact: Over 93% of Suriname is blanketed by pristine tropical rainforest, making it the most heavily forested sovereign country on Earth.
short_desc: UNESCO Dutch wooden architecture of Paramaribo, Central Suriname Nature Reserve rainforest, and harmonious multicultural harmony.

name: Sweden
famous_for: Stockholm Gamla Stan archipelago, IKEA, ABBA, Midsummer flower crowns, Northern Lights in Lapland, and 'Fika' coffee culture.
tourists: Over 7.5M international visitors; famous for Vasa 17th-century warship museum, Icehotel in Jukkasjärvi, and Gothenburg canals.
must_know: 'Fika' is an essential daily ritual: stepping away from work to slow down and connect over hot coffee and fresh cinnamon buns (kanelbullar).
fun_fact: The Stockholm archipelago alone comprises more than 30,000 individual granite islands, islets, and rocky skerries.
short_desc: Stockholm Gamla Stan archipelago, IKEA, ABBA, Midsummer flower crowns, Northern Lights in Lapland, and 'Fika' coffee culture.

name: Switzerland
famous_for: The Matterhorn peak, precision Swiss watches, alpine chocolate, fondue cheese, and scenic trains.
tourists: Over 11.8M visitors; highlights include Jungfraujoch ('Top of Europe'), Lake Geneva, and Glacier Express.
must_know: Sunday is strictly observed as a quiet rest day; loud activities like mowing or vacuuming are discouraged.
fun_fact: Switzerland has enough nuclear fallout shelters to accommodate 100% of its entire national population.
short_desc: The Matterhorn peak, precision Swiss watches, alpine chocolate, fondue cheese, and scenic trains.

name: Syria
famous_for: Damascus (one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on Earth), Roman ruins of Palmyra, and Umayyad Mosque.
tourists: Approx. 1.2M visitors (heritage restoration underway); famous for Umayyad Mosque, Crac des Chevaliers crusader castle, and Aleppo Citadel.
must_know: Damascus has been continuously inhabited for over 11,000 years and is mentioned repeatedly across the earliest recorded histories.
fun_fact: Aleppo soap, made of olive oil and laurel berry oil, has been crafted using unchanged artisanal formulas for thousands of years.
short_desc: Damascus (one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on Earth), Roman ruins of Palmyra, and Umayyad Mosque.

name: Taiwan
famous_for: Taipei 101 skyscraper, vibrant night markets (Shilin), birthplace of Bubble Tea, Taroko Gorge marble canyon, and high-tech semiconductor chips.
tourists: Over 11.8M international visitors; famous for Jiufen mountain lantern village, Sun Moon Lake, and National Palace Museum imperial treasures.
must_know: Taiwan's night market culture is world-famous: eating 'small bites' (xiaochi) while strolling through bustling evening lanes is a daily ritual.
fun_fact: Taipei 101 was the world's tallest building from 2004 to 2010 and contains a massive 660-tonne tuned mass damper pendulum inside its top floors.
short_desc: Taipei 101 skyscraper, vibrant night markets (Shilin), birthplace of Bubble Tea, Taroko Gorge marble canyon, and high-tech semiconductor chi...

name: Tajikistan
famous_for: The Pamir Highway ('Roof of the World' road trip), crystal turquoise lakes of the Fann Mountains, and Silk Road citadels.
tourists: Over 1.0M adventure travelers; famous for Pamir Highway (M41), Iskanderkul alpine lake, and Wakhan Corridor petroglyphs.
must_know: Over 93% of Tajikistan's total territory is mountainous, with more than half the country sitting above 3,000 meters altitude.
fun_fact: The Pamir Highway is the second-highest international highway in the world, cresting the Ak-Baital Pass at 4,655 meters altitude.
short_desc: The Pamir Highway ('Roof of the World' road trip), crystal turquoise lakes of the Fann Mountains, and Silk Road citadels.

name: Tanzania
famous_for: Mount Kilimanjaro (highest peak in Africa, 5,895m), Serengeti Great Migration, Ngorongoro Crater, and Zanzibar spice island beaches.
tourists: Over 1.8M safari and beach visitors; famous for Serengeti lions, Kilimanjaro climbs, Stone Town Zanzibar, and Mafia Island whale sharks.
must_know: 'Pole Pole' (slowly, slowly) is the universal Swahili mantra, especially emphasized when climbing the high altitudes of Kilimanjaro.
fun_fact: The Ngorongoro Crater is the world's largest intact, unflooded volcanic caldera, forming a self-contained sanctuary for 25,000 large animals.
short_desc: Mount Kilimanjaro (highest peak in Africa, 5,895m), Serengeti Great Migration, Ngorongoro Crater, and Zanzibar spice island beaches.

name: Thailand
famous_for: 'Land of Smiles', ornate Grand Palace, floating markets, Pad Thai street food, tropical beaches of Phi Phi, and Songkran water festival.
tourists: Over 28.1M international tourists annually; famous for Wat Arun, Elephant sanctuaries in Chiang Mai, and Railay beach cliffs.
must_know: The head is considered the sacred highest part of the body, so never touch anyone's head; feet are lowest and should never point at Buddha.
fun_fact: Songkran, the Thai New Year in mid-April, transforms the entire nation into the world's biggest friendly water fight celebration.
short_desc: 'Land of Smiles', ornate Grand Palace, floating markets, Pad Thai street food, tropical beaches of Phi Phi, and Songkran water festival.

name: The Bahamas
famous_for: Turquoise waters, swimming pigs of Exuma, pink sand beaches of Harbour Island, and Junkanoo.
tourists: Over 9.6M visitors; famous for Atlantis Paradise Island, Exuma Cays, and Dean's Blue Hole.
must_know: Junkanoo is a vibrant Boxing Day street parade featuring handmade crepe-paper costumes and cowbells.
fun_fact: Dean's Blue Hole in Long Island, Bahamas plunges 202 meters (663 ft), among the world's deepest sinkholes.
short_desc: Turquoise waters, swimming pigs of Exuma, pink sand beaches of Harbour Island, and Junkanoo.

name: The Gambia
famous_for: Nicknamed the 'Smiling Coast of Africa' for warm people, birdwatching along the Gambia River, and Kunta Kinteh Island.
tourists: Over 600,000 visitors; popular for Atlantic beach resorts in Kotu, Bijilo Monkey Park, and riverboat bird tours.
must_know: The Gambia is the smallest sovereign country in mainland Africa, tracing the course of the Gambia River.
fun_fact: Over 540 species of birds inhabit this tiny country, making it a world capital for ornithologists and birdwatchers.
short_desc: Nicknamed the 'Smiling Coast of Africa' for warm people, birdwatching along the Gambia River, and Kunta Kinteh Island.

name: Togo
famous_for: Koutammakou UNESCO fortified clay tower-houses (Takienta), Lomé Grand Marché cloth traders (Nana Benz), and voodoo markets.
tourists: Over 900,000 visitors; famous for Akodessewa Fetish Market, Koutammakou landscape, and Lake Togo pirogues.
must_know: The famous 'Nana Benz' women of Lomé built vast commercial empires in the 1970s controlling West Africa's vibrant wax-print cloth trade.
fun_fact: The Takienta two-story clay tower-houses of the Batammariba people in Koutammakou are living architectural masterpieces of fortified earthen engineering.
short_desc: Koutammakou UNESCO fortified clay tower-houses (Takienta), Lomé Grand Marché cloth traders (Nana Benz), and voodoo markets.

name: Trinidad and Tobago
famous_for: Trinidad Carnival (greatest street party on Earth), birthplace of Steelpan drums, Calypso & Soca music, and Pitch Lake.
tourists: Over 400,000 visitors; famous for Carnival masquerade parades, Pigeon Point in Tobago, and Caroni Bird Sanctuary scarlet ibises.
must_know: The steelpan drum, crafted from 55-gallon oil drums, is the only acoustic musical instrument invented in the 20th century.
fun_fact: Pitch Lake in Trinidad is the largest natural asphalt deposit in the world, supplying tar for famous roads including London's Pall Mall.
short_desc: Trinidad Carnival (greatest street party on Earth), birthplace of Steelpan drums, Calypso & Soca music, and Pitch Lake.

name: Tunisia
famous_for: Ancient Carthage ruins, Star Wars desert sets in Matmata & Tataouine, blue-and-white Sidi Bou Said cliff village, and El Djem amphitheatre.
tourists: Over 9.4M visitors; famous for El Djem Roman amphitheatre, Bardo mosaic museum, Medina of Tunis, and Djerba island synagogues.
must_know: Sidi Bou Said's famous blue-and-white architectural code was established by Baron Rodolphe d'Erlanger in the 1920s.
fun_fact: El Djem's Roman amphitheatre could hold 35,000 spectators and is one of the best-preserved imperial amphitheatres in the Mediterranean.
short_desc: Ancient Carthage ruins, Star Wars desert sets in Matmata & Tataouine, blue-and-white Sidi Bou Said cliff village, and El Djem amphitheatre.

name: Turkey
famous_for: Hagia Sophia, hot air balloons over Cappadocia fairy chimneys, Pamukkale thermal travertine terraces, Turkish tea, and Grand Bazaar.
tourists: Over 50.5M international tourists annually (top 4 globally); famous for Blue Mosque, Ephesus ancient city, and Bosphorus strait.
must_know: Turkish tea (çay) is served in small tulip glasses as a universal symbol of friendship; accepting a cup when offered is customary warmth.
fun_fact: Istanbul is the only metropolis in the world located on two continents simultaneously, spanning both Europe and Asia across the Bosphorus.
short_desc: Hagia Sophia, hot air balloons over Cappadocia fairy chimneys, Pamukkale thermal travertine terraces, Turkish tea, and Grand Bazaar.

name: Turkmenistan
famous_for: Darvaza Gas Crater ('Door to Hell' fiery burning pit), white marble capital city of Ashgabat, and legendary Akhal-Teke horses.
tourists: Approx. 15,000 visitors (regulated transit); famous for Darvaza burning gas crater, ancient Merv Silk Road metropolis, and Nisa ruins.
must_know: Ashgabat holds the official Guinness World Record for having the highest concentration of white marble-clad buildings in the world.
fun_fact: The Darvaza Gas Crater has been burning continuously in the heart of the Karakum Desert since geologists lit it in 1971.
short_desc: Darvaza Gas Crater ('Door to Hell' fiery burning pit), white marble capital city of Ashgabat, and legendary Akhal-Teke horses.

name: Uganda
famous_for: 'Pearl of Africa', half of the world's remaining mountain gorillas in Bwindi Impenetrable Forest, source of the Nile in Jinja, and Rwenzori peaks.
tourists: Over 1.5M visitors; famous for Bwindi gorilla tracking, Queen Elizabeth tree-climbing lions, and white-water rafting the Nile in Jinja.
must_know: Winston Churchill famously coined the title 'The Pearl of Africa' in 1908 after marveling at Uganda's magnificent birds, lakes, and vegetation.
fun_fact: Bwindi Impenetrable National Park protects nearly half of the world's entire remaining wild population of endangered mountain gorillas.
short_desc: 'Pearl of Africa', half of the world's remaining mountain gorillas in Bwindi Impenetrable Forest, source of the Nile in Jinja, and Rwenzori ...

name: Ukraine
famous_for: Golden domes of Kyiv Pechersk Lavra, cobblestones of Lviv, Carpathian mountain wooden churches, sunflower fields, and Vyshyvanka embroidery.
tourists: Over 14.0M visitors (pre-conflict peak); famous for Saint Sophia Cathedral, Tunnel of Love in Klevan, and Black Sea port of Odesa.
must_know: The Vyshyvanka is the intricately embroidered national linen shirt; each Ukrainian region features its own distinctive geometric embroidery pattern.
fun_fact: Arsenalna station on the Kyiv Metro is the deepest metro station in the world, plunging 105.5 meters beneath the earth.
short_desc: Golden domes of Kyiv Pechersk Lavra, cobblestones of Lviv, Carpathian mountain wooden churches, sunflower fields, and Vyshyvanka embroidery.

name: United Arab Emirates
famous_for: Burj Khalifa, Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, futuristic architecture, and luxury desert resorts.
tourists: Over 22.7M visitors; famous for Dubai Mall, Louvre Abu Dhabi, and desert safaris.
must_know: Respect Islamic traditions; dress modestly in public venues and avoid public displays of affection.
fun_fact: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai stands at an astounding 828 meters (2,717 ft), the world's tallest building.
short_desc: Burj Khalifa, Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, futuristic architecture, and luxury desert resorts.

name: United Kingdom
famous_for: Big Ben, Stonehenge, Queen & Royal Family, Shakespeare, The Beatles, afternoon tea, and Premier League.
tourists: Over 38.0M visitors; famous for Tower of London, British Museum, Edinburgh Castle, and Scottish Highlands.
must_know: Queuing in orderly lines is a sacred social rule; jumping a queue is met with severe disapproval.
fun_fact: The British Library in London houses over 170 million items, with three million new items added every single year.
short_desc: Big Ben, Stonehenge, Queen & Royal Family, Shakespeare, The Beatles, afternoon tea, and Premier League.

name: United States
famous_for: Statue of Liberty, Hollywood cinema, Grand Canyon, Yellowstone geysers, Silicon Valley tech, Broadway, Jazz, and Rock 'n' Roll.
tourists: Over 79.3M international tourists annually; famous for Times Square, Golden Gate Bridge, Walt Disney World, and Las Vegas strip.
must_know: Tipping 18-22% at sit-down restaurants is customary and expected, as service staff wages rely heavily on gratuities.
fun_fact: The United States created the world's very first national park when Yellowstone was established by President Ulysses S. Grant in 1872.
short_desc: Statue of Liberty, Hollywood cinema, Grand Canyon, Yellowstone geysers, Silicon Valley tech, Broadway, Jazz, and Rock 'n' Roll.

name: Uruguay
famous_for: Punta del Este luxury coastal resort, Candombe drum rhythms, historic Colonia del Sacramento cobblestones, and world-class grass-fed beef.
tourists: Over 3.2M tourists annually; famous for Casapueblo cliff sculpture house, La Mano finger sculpture in Punta del Este, and Rambla of Montevideo.
must_know: Carrying a thermos under one arm and a mate gourd in hand while walking anywhere is an inseparable part of Uruguayan daily identity.
fun_fact: Uruguay hosted and won the very first FIFA World Cup in 1930 at the Estadio Centenario in Montevideo.
short_desc: Punta del Este luxury coastal resort, Candombe drum rhythms, historic Colonia del Sacramento cobblestones, and world-class grass-fed beef.

name: Uzbekistan
famous_for: Legendary Silk Road oasis cities: Registan of Samarkand, turquoise minarets of Bukhara, walled mud-brick citadel of Khiva, and Plov.
tourists: Over 6.6M international visitors; famous for Registan turquoise madrasahs, Shah-i-Zinda mausoleum avenue, and Chorsu Bazaar.
must_know: Bread (Non) is held in sacred regard; it is torn by hand with both hands and never placed upside down or cut with a knife.
fun_fact: Samarkand is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in Central Asia, flourishing as the glittering capital of the Timurid Empire.
short_desc: Legendary Silk Road oasis cities: Registan of Samarkand, turquoise minarets of Bukhara, walled mud-brick citadel of Khiva, and Plov.

name: Vanuatu
famous_for: Mount Yasur accessible bubbling active volcano on Tanna, ancient land diving (ancestor of bungee jumping), and crystal blue holes of Espiritu Santo.
tourists: Over 120,000 visitors; famous for Mount Yasur volcano crater edge walks, Champagne Beach, and Million Dollar Point dive.
must_know: The land diving ritual (Naghol) on Pentecost Island inspired modern bungee jumping: men leap from 30-meter wooden towers with only vines tied to ankles.
fun_fact: Mount Yasur on Tanna island has been erupting continuously for over 800 years, dubbed the 'Lighthouse of the Pacific' by Captain Cook.
short_desc: Mount Yasur accessible bubbling active volcano on Tanna, ancient land diving (ancestor of bungee jumping), and crystal blue holes of Espirit...

name: Venezuela
famous_for: Angel Falls (world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, 979m), table-top tepui mountains of Canaima, Los Roques coral atolls, and Arepas.
tourists: Approx. 400,000 visitors; famous for Angel Falls (Salto Ángel), Mount Roraima prehistoric plateau, and Catatumbo lightning.
must_know: The Catatumbo Lightning phenomenon over Lake Maracaibo produces up to 280 lightning strikes per hour for up to 160 nights a year.
fun_fact: Angel Falls in Canaima National Park plunges 979 meters (3,212 ft) off Auyán-tepui, roughly 19 times higher than Niagara Falls.
short_desc: Angel Falls (world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, 979m), table-top tepui mountains of Canaima, Los Roques coral atolls, and Arepas.

name: Vietnam
famous_for: Emerald waters of Ha Long Bay, lantern-lit ancient streets of Hoi An, Pho noodle soup, floating Mekong delta markets, and Ao Dai gowns.
tourists: Over 12.6M international visitors; famous for Ha Long Bay junk boats, Golden Bridge in Ba Na Hills, and Son Doong (largest cave on Earth).
must_know: Crossing the street amidst swarms of scooters requires walking at a steady, predictable pace so riders can smoothly maneuver around you.
fun_fact: Son Doong Cave in Phong Nha-Ke Bang is the largest natural cave on Earth, large enough to house an entire 40-story city skyscraper block.
short_desc: Emerald waters of Ha Long Bay, lantern-lit ancient streets of Hoi An, Pho noodle soup, floating Mekong delta markets, and Ao Dai gowns.

name: Western Sahara
famous_for: Vast Atlantic-meets-Sahara sand dunes, world-class kitesurfing in Dakhla lagoon, camel trekking, and nomadic tent traditions.
tourists: Approx. 120,000 adventure travelers; famous for Dakhla kitesurfing camps, White Dune of Dakhla, and Atlantic fishing.
must_know: The Hassaniya tea ceremony requires three distinct glasses of sweet frothy tea: the first is bitter like life, second sweet like love, third gentle like death.
fun_fact: Dakhla lagoon boasts 300+ days of consistent ocean wind annually, transforming it into a world-famous kiteboarding mecca.
short_desc: Vast Atlantic-meets-Sahara sand dunes, world-class kitesurfing in Dakhla lagoon, camel trekking, and nomadic tent traditions.

name: Yemen
famous_for: Dragon's Blood trees on Socotra Island, UNESCO mud-brick skyscrapers of Shibam ('Manhattan of the Desert'), and gingerbread houses of Sana'a.
tourists: Approx. 20,000 visitors (mostly Socotra eco-travelers); famous for Socotra dragon trees, Old City of Sana'a, and Mocha coffee heritage.
must_know: Shibam in Wadi Hadramawt features 16th-century mud-brick tower apartments rising up to 11 stories, the oldest vertical urban skyscrapers on Earth.
fun_fact: Socotra Island in the Arabian Sea is nicknamed the 'Galapagos of the Indian Ocean' because one-third of its plant species exist nowhere else.
short_desc: Dragon's Blood trees on Socotra Island, UNESCO mud-brick skyscrapers of Shibam ('Manhattan of the Desert'), and gingerbread houses of Sana'a...

name: Zambia
famous_for: Victoria Falls ('Mosi-oa-Tunya' - The Smoke That Thunders), Devil's Pool swimming on the waterfall edge, and South Luangwa safari.
tourists: Over 1.2M safari visitors; famous for Victoria Falls bridge bungee, walking safaris in South Luangwa, and Lower Zambezi canoeing.
must_know: Zambia pioneered the concept of the walking safari in South Luangwa, allowing travelers to track elephants and leopards on foot with armed guides.
fun_fact: Victoria Falls is one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World, forming the largest sheet of falling water on the planet.
short_desc: Victoria Falls ('Mosi-oa-Tunya' - The Smoke That Thunders), Devil's Pool swimming on the waterfall edge, and South Luangwa safari.

name: Zimbabwe
famous_for: Great Zimbabwe stone ruins (medieval stone palace that gave the nation its name), Victoria Falls, and Hwange elephant herds.
tourists: Over 2.3M tourists annually; famous for Victoria Falls rainforest trails, Great Zimbabwe stone monuments, and Mana Pools canoeing.
must_know: The name 'Zimbabwe' comes from the Shona phrase 'Dzimba-dza-mabwe', meaning 'large houses of stone', after the ancient dry-stone empire ruins.
fun_fact: Great Zimbabwe was a medieval stone city constructed without a single drop of mortar between the 11th and 15th centuries.
short_desc: Great Zimbabwe stone ruins (medieval stone palace that gave the nation its name), Victoria Falls, and Hwange elephant herds.
